BURSEVI:v10p317/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p317/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p317/r9.claim: Remembering God's name means inwardly and outwardly; prayer means the five prescribed prayers, beginning with the opening takbir, while Hanafi usage includes all forms of remembrance.
BURSEVI:v10p317/r9.anchor: {وذكر اسم ربه} بقلبه ولسانه {فصلى} أقام الصلوات الخمس

BURSEVI:v10p317/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p317/r10.speaker: الإمام
BURSEVI:v10p317/r10.claim: The Imam orders the deeds as purifying false beliefs, recalling knowledge of God through His names and attributes, and serving through prayer and bodily obedience.
BURSEVI:v10p317/r10.anchor: قال الامام مراتب أعمال المكلف ثلاث فأولاها إزالة العقائد الفاسدة عن القلب

BURSEVI:v10p318/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p318/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p318/r4.claim: Another gloss says the purified person repents, hears the call to prayer, and goes out to pray; the next verse rebukes those who choose worldly work instead.
BURSEVI:v10p318/r4.anchor: ويقال قد أفلح من تزكى أي من تاب من الذنوب وذكر اسم ربه يعني إذا سمع الأذان خرج إلى الصلاة

QASHANI:87:13-15/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:87:13-15/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:87:13-15/r3.claim: Remembering the nurturing name means invoking the particular name that grants the perfection one’s innate readiness seeks, such as Knower for the ignorant, Guide for the astray, or Forgiver for the sinner; it is truly the essence hidden by effects and self-qualities.
QASHANI:87:13-15/r3.anchor: الاسم الخاص الذي يربه به بإفاضة كماله الذي يسأل ربه بلسان استعداده كالعليم للجاهل والهادي للضال والغفار للمذنب

QASHANI:87:13-15/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:87:13-15/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:87:13-15/r4.claim: Remembering is knowing God and seeking one’s particular perfection through divine aid; prayer is worship of the Real disclosed in the form of that name after one sees its destined perfection. The verse about forgetting God explains self-forgetting.
QASHANI:87:13-15/r4.anchor: وذكره تعرفه وطلب كماله المخصوص به بالتأييد الرباني والتوفيق الإلهي

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says remembering God's name means affirming His oneness, and prayer means the five prayers.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r2.anchor: وذكر اسم ربه قال : وحد الله فصلى قال : الصلوات الخمس

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r7.claim: A report explicitly graded weak says the Prophet commanded paying zakat al-fitr before Eid prayer and recited these verses; another wording identifies the verse's purification with zakat al-fitr.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r7.anchor: بسند ضعيف عن كثير بن عبد الله بن عمرو بن عوف ، عن أبيه ، عن جده ، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم انه كان يامر بزكاة الفطر

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r9.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r9.claim: Ibn Sirin says the person paid the fitr charity, then went out and prayed.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r9.anchor: عن محمد بن سيرين رضي الله عنه في قوله : قد افلح من تزكى قال : ادى صدقة الفطر ثم خرج فصلى

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r13.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r13.speaker: أبو الأحوص
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r13.claim: Abu al-Ahwas says a person who gives charity may pray two units and then recite this verse.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r13.anchor: عن أبي الاحوص رضي الله عنه قال : لو ان الذي يتصدق بالصدقة صلى ركعتين ثم قرا قد افلح من تزكى

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r14.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r14.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r14.claim: Ibn Masud says one setting out for prayer may give charity, linking the act with the verse's sequence of purification and prayer.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3417#3/r14.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال : اذا خرج احدكم يريد الصلاة فلا عليه ان يتصدق بشئ لان الله يقول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r4.claim: A report from the Prophet via Jabir explains purification as professing God's oneness, rejecting partners, and affirming the Prophet's mission.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r4.anchor: أخرج البزار عن جابر بن عبدالله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : { قد أفلح من تزكى } قال : من شهد أن لا إلاه إلا الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ata, Ikrima, and Qatada identify the prayer as the five prescribed prayers, carefully maintained.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r5.anchor: وذكر اسم ربه فصلى } قال : هي الصلوات الخمس والمحافظة عليها والاهتمام بها ، وهو قول ابن عباس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r6.claim: Purification comes first because it is the foundation of the subsequent work: a cleansed soul receives guidance and turns more readily to good.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r6.anchor: وقدم التزكي على ذكر الله والصلاة لأنه أصل العمل بذلك كله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r7.claim: On one reading, remembering the Lord's name is spoken remembrance of God's names and exaltation, such as the testimony, takbir, and tasbih.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p287/r7.anchor: وفعل { ذكر اسم ربه } يجوز أن يكون من الذكر اللساني الذي هو بكسر الذال فيكون كلمة { اسم ربه }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p288/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p288/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p288/r1.claim: Alternatively, dhikr is inward recollection, with “name” pointing to God's character and attributes of perfection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p288/r1.anchor: من الذكر بضم الذال وهو حضور الشيء في النفس الذاكرة والمفكرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p288/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p288/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p288/r2.claim: Prayer follows remembrance in either sense because remembering God prompts reverence and closeness through prayer, which combines submission and praise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p288/r2.anchor: وتفريع { فصلى } على { ذكر اسم ربه } على كلا الوجهين لأن الذكر بمعنييه يبعث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p288/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p288/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p288/r3.claim: The three qualities unfold in order: purifying false beliefs, recalling God's perfection with fear and hope, then obeying and worshipping; prayer represents worship and leads to other deeds.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p288/r3.anchor: وقد رتبت هذه الخصال الثلاث على الآية على ترتيب تولدها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r5.claim: Remembering the Lord means affirming God's oneness; prayer includes the obligatory prayers and whatever voluntary prayer and good works one can manage.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r5.anchor: وذكر اسم ربه معناه: وحده وصلى له الصلوات التي فرضت عليه، وتنفل أيضا بما أمكنه من صلاة وبر،

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#4/r1.claim: The meaning of remembering the Lord's name was explained earlier at 33:31.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#4/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#4/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#4/r2.claim: One view says the prayer is the five obligatory prayers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#4/r2.anchor: أحدها أنها الصلوات الخمس قاله ابن عباس ومقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#4/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#4/r3.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#4/r3.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī identifies the prayer as the two Eid prayers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#4/r3.anchor: والثاني صلاة العيدين قاله أبو سعيد الخدري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#4/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#4/r4.speaker: أبو الأحوص
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#4/r4.claim: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ says the prayer is voluntary worship.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#4/r4.anchor: والثالث صلاة التطوع قاله أبو الأحوص

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#4/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#4/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#4/r5.claim: The Ibn ʿAbbās interpretation is preferred for both verses: this sūra is Meccan by consensus, and there was no alms or Eid prayer in Mecca.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#4/r5.anchor: والقول قول ابن عباس في الآيتين فإن هذه السورة مكية بلا خلاف ولم يكن بمكة زكاة ولا عيد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p381/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p381/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p381/r2.claim: Remembering the Lord's name and praying means keeping the prayers at their prescribed times in pursuit of God's approval and obedience to His law.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p381/r2.anchor: أي: أقام الصلاة في أوقاتها؛ ابتغاء رضوان الله وطاعة لأمر الله وامتثالا لشرع الله.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p381/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p381/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p381/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the prayer as the five prescribed prayers, and Ibn Jarir chooses this interpretation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p381/r4.anchor: وكذا قال ابن عباس: إن المراد بذلك الصلوات الخمس. واختاره ابن جرير.

JISHUMI:v10p7378/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7378/r6.speaker: أبي العالية وأبي سعيد الخدري وابن عمر
JISHUMI:v10p7378/r6.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya, Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, and Ibn ʿUmar connect purification with the alms of fast-breaking and the Eid prayer; Ibn ʿUmar would check that Nafiʿ had paid before leaving for prayer.
JISHUMI:v10p7378/r6.anchor: عن أبي العالية، وأبي سعيد الخدري، وابن عمر

JISHUMI:v10p7380/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r10.speaker: أبي ذر
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r10.claim: Abū Dharr asked the Prophet what the earlier scriptures contained; the Prophet answered by reciting these two verses.
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r10.anchor: وعن أبي ذر، قلت: يا رسول الله، ما كان في الصحف الأولى؟

JISHUMI:v10p7380/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r14.claim: Paradise is attained through the combined deeds named: purification consists of performing obligations and avoiding grave sins; purification, prayer, and remembrance are human actions.
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r14.anchor: والتطهير إنما يحصل بأداء الواجبات واجتناب الكبائر

KASHSHAF:87:15/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:15/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:15/r1.claim: One explanation takes the prayer to mean the five daily prayers.

KASHSHAF:87:15/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:15/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
KASHSHAF:87:15/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿud prayed for God's mercy on a woman who gave charity and prayed.
KASHSHAF:87:15/r2.anchor: عن ابن مسعود : رحم الله امرأة تصدق وصلى

KASHSHAF:87:15/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:15/r3.speaker: علي
KASHSHAF:87:15/r3.claim: Ali identifies purification with alms at the end of Ramadan and connects it to going to the prayer ground, Eid prayer, and the opening takbir.
KASHSHAF:87:15/r3.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه أنه التصدق بصدقة الفطر

KASHSHAF:87:15/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:15/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:15/r4.claim: The sequence is evidence that the opening takbir is obligatory, outside the prayer itself because prayer is conjoined to it, and may use any divine name.
KASHSHAF:87:15/r4.anchor: وذكر اسم ربه فكبر تكبيرة الافتتاح

KASHSHAF:87:15/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:15/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF:87:15/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the person recalled the return and standing before God, then prayed to Him.
KASHSHAF:87:15/r5.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه : ذكر معاده وموقفه

KASHSHAF:87:15/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:15/r6.speaker: الضحاك
KASHSHAF:87:15/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak says he remembered God on the way to the prayer ground and performed the Eid prayer.
KASHSHAF:87:15/r6.anchor: وعن الضحاك : وذكر اسم ربه في طريق المصلى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742/r2.claim: Fa-salla may mean the five prayers; reports explain it as almsgiving and prayer, remembering one's return to God before praying, or remembering God on the way to the Eid prayer.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742/r2.anchor: أي الصلوات الخمس ، نحو قوله : { ليس البر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742/r3.speaker: علي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742/r3.claim: Ali interprets the successful person's purification as paying zakat al-fitr before going to the Eid prayer; he says he is content if his record contains no more than this proof.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742/r3.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه التصدق بصدقة الفطر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742/r4.claim: The sequence is evidence that the opening takbir is obligatory, precedes and is not part of prayer, and may use any of God's names.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742/r4.anchor: وبه يحتج على وجوب تكبيرة الافتتاح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the worshipper remembers the return and standing before the Lord, then prays to Him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742/r5.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه : ذكر معاده وموقفه بين يدي ربه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742/r6.speaker: الضحاك
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak says the person remembers God's name on the way to the prayer ground and performs the Eid prayer.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742/r6.anchor: وعن الضحاك : وذكر اسم ربه في طريق المصلى

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r5.claim: He interprets remembering the Lord's name as affirming God's unity.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r5.anchor: أن يوحد الله , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r6.claim: Another meaning is calling upon God and directing one's desire to Him.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r7.claim: Another meaning is seeking forgiveness and repenting to God.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r8.claim: One interpretation is inward recollection during prayer, producing fear of punishment and hope for reward, and therefore full attention and humility.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r9.claim: Another interpretation is verbally mentioning God's name at the start of prayer, since prayer is not valid without it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r9.anchor: بصلاته , لأنها لا تنعقد إلا بذكره

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r10.claim: A further interpretation is opening each sura with the basmala.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r11.claim: He says fa-salla refers to the five daily prayers.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r12.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r12.claim: He says fa-salla refers to the Eid prayer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r12.anchor: صلاة العيد , قاله أبو سعيد الخدري

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r13.speaker: أبو الأحوص
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r13.claim: He interprets it as performing a voluntary prayer after paying alms.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r13.anchor: يتطوع بصلاة بعد زكاة , قاله أبو الأحوص

MUQATIL:87:14-19/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:87:14-19/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:87:14-19/r1.claim: The successful person pays alms, bears witness that there is no god but God, and performs the five daily prayers.
MUQATIL:87:14-19/r1.anchor: قد أفلح من أدى الزكاة، وشهد أن لا إله إلا الله، وصلى الصلوات الخمس

NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#4/r1.claim: Remembering the Lord's name means saying the opening takbir and then performing the five prayers.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#4/r1.anchor: ﴿ وذكر اسم ربه ﴾ وكبر للافتتاح ﴿ فصلى ﴾ الخمس

NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#4/r2.claim: This is evidence that the opening takbir is obligatory, distinct from the prayer because prayer is coordinated with it, and may use any of God's names.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#4/r2.anchor: وبه يحتج على وجوب تكبيرة الافتتاح وعلى أنها ليست من الصلاة لأن الصلاة عطفت عليها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#4/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#4/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets remembrance as recalling the return and standing before one's Lord, followed by prayer to Him.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#4/r3.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما ذكر معاده وموقفه بين يدى ربه فصلى له

NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#4/r4.speaker: الضحاك
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#4/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets remembrance as invoking God's name on the way to the prayer place, followed by the Eid prayer.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#4/r4.anchor: وعن الضحاك وذكر اسم ربه فى طريق المصلى فصلى صلاة العيد

QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r4.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r4.claim: Remembering God recalls the return and standing before Him, leading one to worship and pray.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r4.anchor: وروى عطاء عن ابن عباس قال: يرد ذكر معاده وموقفه بين يدي الله

QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r5.claim: Remembering God's name is the opening takbir; this supports its obligation and its being outside the prayer, since prayer is coordinated after it.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: ذكر اسم ربه بالتكبير في أول الصلاة، لأنها لا تنعقد إلا بذكره

QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r6.claim: The same proof is used for permitting the opening takbir with any of God's names, a disputed issue among jurists.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r6.anchor: وفيه حجة لمن قال: إن الافتتاح جائز بكل اسم من أسماء الله عز وجل

QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r7.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r7.claim: He interprets the remembrance on the way to the prayer ground and the prayer as the Eid takbirs and Eid prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r7.anchor: قال الضحاك: «وذكر اسم ربه» في طريق المصلى «فصلى» أي صلاة العيد

QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r8.claim: Remembrance may be inward during prayer, prompting fear of punishment and hope for reward, and thus complete observance and humility.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r8.anchor: وقيل: { وذكر اسم ربه } وهو أن يذكره بقلبه عند صلاته

QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r9.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r9.claim: Another reading takes the remembrance as beginning each surah with the basmala; prayer and remembrance need not occur in the stated order.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r9.anchor: هو أن يفتتح أول كل سورة ببسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r10.claim: The conjunction does not require chronology, as in saying either that someone honored then visited me or visited then honored me.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r10.anchor: ولا فرق بين أن تقول: أكرمتني فزرتني، وبين أن تقول: زرتني فأكرمتني

QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r11.claim: He identifies the prayer as the five obligatory prayers.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r11.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هذا في الصلاة المفروضة، وهي الصلوات الخمس

QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r12.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r12.claim: Prayer may mean supplication to God for worldly and afterlife needs.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r12.anchor: وقيل: الدعاء أي دعاء الله بحوائج الدنيا والآخرة

QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r13.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري وابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r13.claim: They also identify the prayer as the Eid prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r13.anchor: وقيل: صلاة العيد قاله أبو سعيد الخدري وابن عمر وغيرهما

QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r14.speaker: أبو الأحوص
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r14.claim: He understands the prayer as voluntary prayer after paying zakat; this also follows from Ata's interpretation.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r14.anchor: وقيل: هو أن يتطوع بصلاة بعد زكاته قاله أبو الأحوص

QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r15.speaker: عبد الله
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r15.claim: He says that one who performs prayer but does not pay zakat has no prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:14-15#2/r15.anchor: وروي عن عبد الله قال: من أقام الصلاة ولم يؤت الزكاة فلا صلاة له

NAHHAS:v5p207/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p207/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v5p207/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says fa-ṣallā refers to performing the five prayers.
NAHHAS:v5p207/r4.anchor: روى ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس قال وحده قال ( فصلى ) يقول فصلى الصلوات الخمس

NAHHAS:v5p207/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p207/r5.speaker: غيره
NAHHAS:v5p207/r5.claim: Another interpreter says ṣallā here means he supplicated.

NAHHAS:v5p207/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p207/r6.speaker: محمد بن جرير
NAHHAS:v5p207/r6.claim: Muḥammad ibn Jarīr understands the person as praying and mentioning the Lord through praise and glorification in prayer.
NAHHAS:v5p207/r6.anchor: والصواب عند محمد بن جرير أن يكون المعنى صلى فذكر اسم ربه في صلاته بالتحميد والتمجيد

NAHHAS:v5p207/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p207/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p207/r7.claim: The author rejects Ibn Jarīr's syntax because it makes what precedes the conjunction occur after it, reversing normal grammatical sequence.
NAHHAS:v5p207/r7.anchor: قال أبو جعفر وهذا غلط على قول أهل العربية لأنه جعل ما قبل الفاء بعدها

NAHHAS:v5p207/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p207/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p207/r8.claim: The author prefers Ibn ʿAbbās's interpretation of ṣallā as the five prayers.

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.claim: Al-Aʿla is Meccan and has nineteen verses; the Prophet loved it, recited it at Eid and Friday prayers with al-Ghashiya, sometimes on the same day.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.anchor: سورة الأعلى مكية وآياتها تسع عشرة

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.claim: The surah turns the entire cosmos into a sanctuary reverberating with praise and offers the Prophet good news of divine preservation and ease in his mission and affairs.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.anchor: وحق لرسول الله [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] أن يحب هذه السورة وهي تحيل له الكون كله معبدا

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.claim: Its foundations are God's oneness as creator, divine revelation, and afterlife recompense, rooted in earlier scriptures; it also portrays the easy nature of the message, messenger, and community.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.anchor: وهي تتضمن الثابت من قواعد التصور الإيماني

QUTB-ZILAL:87:10/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:10/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:10/r1.claim: The Prophet fulfills his duty by reminding; people then diverge in response and outcome, and God deals with them according to how they receive the reminder.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:10/r1.anchor: فإذا نهض [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] بهذا العبء فقد أدى ما عليه

QUTB-ZILAL:87:15/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:15/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:15/r1.claim: Remembering God's name means inwardly recalling His majesty; “then he prayed” may mean humble devotion and submission.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:15/r1.anchor: فاستحضر في قلبه جلاله : ( فصلى ) . . إما بمعنى خشع وقنت

QUTB-ZILAL:87:15/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:15/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:15/r2.claim: Alternatively, “then he prayed” may mean canonical ritual prayer; either sense can arise from inward remembrance, awareness of God's majesty, and reverence.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:15/r2.anchor: فكلاهما يمكن أن ينشأ من التذكر

QUTB-ZILAL:87:15/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:15/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:15/r3.claim: One who purifies, remembers, and prays certainly prospers: in this life through a living connection and the sweetness of remembrance, and in the next through escape from Hell and attaining bliss and approval.

RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says remembering God’s name means recalling resurrection and standing before Him, then praying; al-Razi deems this interpretation determinate.
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس : ذكر معاده وموقفه بين يدي ربه فصلى له . وأقول : هذا التفسير متعين

RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r2.claim: The sequence describes three stages: removing false beliefs, knowing God through His names and attributes, then serving Him through humble prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r2.anchor: فالمرتبة الأولى : هي المراد بالتزكية في قوله : { قد أفلح من تزكى

RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r3.speaker: عكرمة، أبو العالية، ابن سيرين، ابن عمر
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r3.claim: A group interprets the passage as charity before Eid followed by Eid prayer; this is also reported from the Prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r3.anchor: وهذا قول عكرمة وأبي العالية وابن سيرين وابن عمر وروي ذلك مرفوعا إلى النبي

RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r4.claim: That Eid interpretation faces the Qur’an’s usual order of prayer before alms and the sura’s Meccan setting, where neither Eid nor fitra existed.
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r4.anchor: أن عادة الله تعالى في القرآن تقديم ذكر الصلاة على ذكر الزكاة

RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r5.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r5.claim: Al-Wahidi answers that God may praise people in advance for practices He knows will occur later.
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r5.anchor: لا يمتنع أن يقال : لما كان في معلوم الله تعالى أن ذلك سيكون أثنى على من فعل ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r6.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r6.claim: Muqatil reads the first phrase as giving alms and the second as affirming oneness in prayer; unlike the Eid view, this concerns obligatory alms and prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r6.anchor: قال مقاتل : { قد أفلح من تزكى } ( الأعلى : 14 ) أي تصدق من ماله

RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r8.claim: A further report says the worshipper proclaims God’s greatness while going out to Eid, then performs the Eid prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس : { وذكر اسم ربه } أي كبر في خروجه إلى العيد وصلى صلاة العيد

RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r9.claim: Another interpretation is remembrance within prayer, unlike hypocrites who perform for show and remember God only a little.
RAZI-FULL:v31p134/r9.anchor: وذكر اسم ربه في صلاته ولا تكون صلاته كصلاة المنافقين حيث يراؤون الناس

RAZI-FULL:v31p134#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p134#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p134#2/r1.claim: Jurists cite this verse as evidence that the opening takbīr is obligatory.
RAZI-FULL:v31p134#2/r1.anchor: الفقهاء احتجوا بهذه الآية على وجوب تكبيرة الافتتاح

RAZI-FULL:v31p134#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p134#2/r2.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v31p134#2/r2.claim: Abu Hanifa argues that opening takbīr is outside prayer because coordination marks distinct things, and that any divine name may open prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v31p134#2/r2.anchor: واحتج أبو حنيفة رحمه الله بها على أن تكبيرة الافتتاح ليست من الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v31p134#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p134#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p134#2/r3.claim: The response notes that the implied order could be pray and then remember, since reversing the order of clauses can preserve the sense.
RAZI-FULL:v31p134#2/r3.anchor: تقدير الآية ، وصلى فذكر اسم ربه ولا فرق بين أن تقول أكرمتني فزرتني

RAZI-FULL:v31p134#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p134#2/r4.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v31p134#2/r4.claim: Abu Hanifa objects that the sequential force of the fāʾ cannot be set aside without evidence.
RAZI-FULL:v31p134#2/r4.anchor: ترك العمل بفاء التعقيب لا يجوز من غير دليل

RAZI-FULL:v31p134#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p134#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p134#2/r5.claim: The verse praises anyone who remembers God and then prays but never identifies that remembrance as the opening takbīr; reflection on reward and punishment may instead prompt prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v31p134#2/r5.anchor: الآية تدل على مدح كل من ذكر اسم الله فصلى عقيبه وليس في الآية بيان أن ذلك الذكر هو تكبيرة الافتتاح

STUDYQURAN:87:14/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:14/r4.speaker: Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq
STUDYQURAN:87:14/r4.claim: The sixth Imam says the verse order refers to alms being given in the morning before the two cycles of the ʿĪd prayer.
STUDYQURAN:87:14/r4.anchor: the sixth Imam, Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq, stated that the order of the verses refers to the alms being given in the morning

STUDYQURAN:87:14/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:14/r5.speaker: most commentators
STUDYQURAN:87:14/r5.claim: Prayer here is usually understood as the five canonical prayers.
STUDYQURAN:87:14/r5.anchor: Here prayer is taken by most as a reference to the five canonical prayers

STUDYQURAN:87:14/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:14/r6.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:87:14/r6.claim: Some instead understand prayer as the congregational prayer on the morning of ʿĪd al-fiṭr.
STUDYQURAN:87:14/r6.anchor: by some as a reference to the congregational prayer said on the morning of ʿĪd al-fiṭr

STUDYQURAN:87:14/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:14/r7.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:87:14/r7.claim: Remembering God's Name can mean uttering the basmalah at the beginning of each prayer.
STUDYQURAN:87:14/r7.anchor: According to some, remembers the Name of his Lord refers to mentioning the Name of God in the basmalah at the beginning of each prayer

STUDYQURAN:87:14/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:14/r8.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:87:14/r8.claim: Others stress that remembrance must engage both heart and tongue; tongue-only remembrance without attention of heart has no benefit or reward.
STUDYQURAN:87:14/r8.anchor: others emphasize that it means to remember with both heart and tongue, as remembering God with the tongue while being heedless of God in the heart has no benefit

STUDYQURAN:87:14/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:14/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:87:14/r9.claim: Read together, the verses describe whole-person worship: purifying the heart, remembering God with the tongue, and performing God's commands, especially prayer.
STUDYQURAN:87:14/r9.anchor: These two verses can be taken together as referring to worshipping with all aspects of one’s being

TAB:87:19/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:19/r6.speaker: author
TAB:87:19/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers that the demonstrative covers the nearby verses about purification, prayer, preferring this life, and the better, lasting afterlife, since this is the nearest referent; ṣuḥuf means the books of Abraham and Moses.
TAB:87:19/r6.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصواب ،   قول من قال :  إن قوله :  قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكى وَذَكَرَ اسمَ رَبّهِ فَصَلّى

TAB-FULL:v24p321/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p321/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p321/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says remembering the Lord’s name means affirming His oneness.
TAB-FULL:v24p321/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، " {وذكر اسم ربه فصلى} [الأعلى: 15] يقول: وحد الله سبحانه وتعالى "

TAB-FULL:v24p321/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p321/r2.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v24p321/r2.claim: Others say the verse means remembering God, calling on Him, and seeking His favor.
TAB-FULL:v24p321/r2.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل معنى ذلك: وذكر الله ودعاه ورغب إليه.

TAB-FULL:v24p321/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p321/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p321/r3.claim: Ṭabarī combines both interpretations: remembering God includes affirming His unity, invoking Him, and seeking Him, with no restriction to one kind of remembrance.
TAB-FULL:v24p321/r3.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك: أن يقال: وذكر الله فوحده، ودعاه ورغب إليه

TAB-FULL:v24p322/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p322/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p322/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes “then prayed” to mean performing the five daily prayers.
TAB-FULL:v24p322/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: " {فصلى} [الأعلى: 15] يقول: صلى الصلوات الخمس "

TAB-FULL:v24p322/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p322/r2.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v24p322/r2.claim: Another view applies the prayer to the Eid al-Fiṭr prayer.
TAB-FULL:v24p322/r2.anchor: وقال آخرون: عني به: صلاة العيد يوم الفطر

TAB-FULL:v24p322/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p322/r3.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v24p322/r3.claim: Others understand prayer here as calling on God, that is, supplication.
TAB-FULL:v24p322/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل عني به: وذكر اسم ربه فدعا؛ وقالوا: الصلاة هاهنا: الدعاء.

TAB-FULL:v24p322/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p322/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p322/r4.claim: Ṭabarī prefers prayer generally, including remembrance through praise, glorification, and supplication within it.
TAB-FULL:v24p322/r4.anchor: والصواب من القول أن يقال: عني بقوله: {فصلى} [الأعلى: 15] : الصلوات، وذكر الله فيها بالتحميد

TAB-FULL:v24p323/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p323/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p323/r6.claim: Ṭabarī prefers that “this” refers to the nearest preceding lines, 87:14–17, because a demonstrative most naturally points to what is nearby; ṣuḥuf means books or scrolls.
TAB-FULL:v24p323/r6.anchor: وإنما قلت: ذلك أولى بالصحة من غيره، لأن هذا إشارة إلى حاضر، فلأن يكون إشارة إلى ما قرب منها

TABATABAI:87:14/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:14/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:14/r1.claim: The opening of the sūra is Meccan, but its closing verses about purification, alms, and Eid prayer were revealed in Medina after those practices were legislated; reports calling the whole sūra Meccan can refer to its opening.
TABATABAI:87:14/r1.anchor: وسياق الآيات في صدر السورة سياق مكي وأما ذيلها أعني قوله { قد أفلح من تزكى } الخ

TABATABAI:87:14-16/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r12.claim: The apparent sense is verbal remembrance of God followed by the prescribed Islamic prayer.
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r12.anchor: الظاهر أن المراد بالذكر الذكر اللفظي، وبالصلاة التوجه الخاص المشروع في الإسلام

TABATABAI:87:14-16/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r13.claim: Although the verses read generally, reports from the Imams and Sunni transmitters identify them with alms of breaking the fast and Eid prayer.
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r13.anchor: والآيتان بحسب ظاهر مدلولهما على العموم لكن ورد في المأثور عن أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام أنهما نزلتا في زكاة الفطر وصلاة العيد

TABATABAI:87:17-19/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r10.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r10.claim: Al-Ṣādiq explains purification as paying alms of breaking the fast and the prayer as going to the prayer ground for Eid prayer; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī notes parallel reports, including an abbreviated one from al-Qummī.
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r10.anchor: وفي الفقيه وسئل الصادق عليه السلام عن قول الله عز وحل { قد أفلح من تزكى } قال قال من أخرج الفطرة

TABATABAI:87:17-19/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r11.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r11.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī reports that the Prophet would recite these verses and distribute fitra before going to the Eid prayer-ground; similar reports are attributed to several early authorities and to the Prophet through ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf.
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r11.anchor: وفي الدر المنثور أخرج ابن مردويه عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يقول { قد أفلح من تزكى

TABRISI:87:10-17/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:10-17/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:87:10-17/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses remembrance of the Lord's name as declaring God's oneness.
TABRISI:87:10-17/r13.anchor: أي وحد الله عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:87:10-17/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:10-17/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:10-17/r14.claim: Another view places remembrance in the heart during prayer, where fear of punishment and hope of reward shape humility.
TABRISI:87:10-17/r14.anchor: ذكر الله بقلبه عند صلاته فرجا ثوابه وخاف عقابه فإن الخشوع في الصلاة بحسب الخوف والرجاء

TABRISI:87:10-17/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:10-17/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:10-17/r15.claim: A further view makes it spoken remembrance at prayer's opening: saying Allāhu akbar, without which prayer does not begin.
TABRISI:87:10-17/r15.anchor: ذكر اسم ربه بلسانه عند دخوله في الصلاة فصلى بذلك الاسم أي قال الله أكبر

TABRISI:87:10-17/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:10-17/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:10-17/r16.claim: Another interpretation is that one begins with the basmala and performs the five prescribed prayers.
TABRISI:87:10-17/r16.anchor: هو أن يفتتح ببسم الله الرحمن الرحيم ويصلي الصلوات الخمس المكتوبة

THALABI:v10p184#3/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p184#3/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
THALABI:v10p184#3/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd prayed for the person who gives charity, then prays, and recited these verses.
THALABI:v10p184#3/r5.anchor: وكان ابن مسعود يقول: رحم الله امرءا تصدق ثم صلى ثم يقرأ هذه الآية

THALABI:v10p184#3/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p184#3/r7.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
THALABI:v10p184#3/r7.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī says the person gives the alms of breaking the fast, goes out for Eid, and prays.
THALABI:v10p184#3/r7.anchor:
قال:
أعطى صدقة الفطر.
وذكر اسم ربه فصلى قال: خرج إلى العيد فصلى

THALABI:v10p184#3/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p184#3/r8.speaker: ابن عمر
THALABI:v10p184#3/r8.claim: Ibn ʿUmar waited for confirmation that the charity had been sent before leaving for the Eid prayer ground; the author reports this as the occasion of the verse.
THALABI:v10p184#3/r8.anchor: كان ابن عمر إذا صلى الغداة- يعني من يوم العيد- قال: يا نافع أخرجت الصدقة

THALABI:v10p184#3/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p184#3/r9.speaker: أبو العالية
THALABI:v10p184#3/r9.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya checked that the visitor had washed and dispatched his alms before Eid prayer, then said the people of Medina know no better charity than that and providing water.
THALABI:v10p184#3/r9.anchor: إن أهل المدينة لا يرون صدقة أفضل منها ومن سقاية الماء

THALABI:v10p184#3/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p184#3/r10.speaker: رسول الله
THALABI:v10p184#3/r10.claim: A prophetic report explains purification as paying the alms of breaking the fast and going out to the prayer ground to pray.
THALABI:v10p184#3/r10.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله: قد أفلح من تزكى قال: «أخرج زكاة الفطر

THALABI:v10p185/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p185/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p185/r1.claim: The author questions the Eid and fitra interpretation because the sura is Meccan by consensus, before there was an Eid or fitra alms in Mecca.
THALABI:v10p185/r1.anchor: قلت: ولا أدري ما وجه هذا التأويل، لأن هذه السورة مكية بالإجماع ولم يكن بمكة عيد

THALABI:v10p185/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p185/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p185/r2.claim: ‘Remembered His name’ may mean remembered God Himself or pronounced His name; prayer may mean Eid takbīr and Eid prayer, the five daily prayers, or supplication.
THALABI:v10p185/r2.anchor: وذكر اسم ربه: أي وذكر ربه، وقيل: وذكر تسمية ربه، وقيل: هو تكبير العيد

THALABI:v10p185/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p185/r3.speaker: رسول الله
THALABI:v10p185/r3.claim: A report from Jābir interprets purification as professing God's oneness, abandoning idols, and affirming the Prophet; prayer is the five prayers, maintained at the call and their appointed times.
THALABI:v10p185/r3.anchor:
قال: «من شهد أن لا إله إلا الله وخلع الأنداد وشهد أني رسول
الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p443/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p443/r11.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p443/r11.claim: Remembering the Lord means recalling the return and standing before God, then praying the five prayers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p443/r11.anchor: ذكر معاده، وموقفه بين يدي الله فصلى

WAHIDI-QT:87:15/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:87:15/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:87:15/r1.claim: Remembering the Lord and praying refers to the five prescribed prayers.
WAHIDI-QT:87:15/r1.anchor: { وذكر اسم ربه فصلى } أي الصلوات الخمس

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:7-16/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:7-16/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:7-16/r11.claim: Remembering the Lord's name and praying refers to the five daily prayers.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:7-16/r11.anchor: وذكر اسم ربه فصلى } أي: الصلوات الخمس.

ELMALILI:87:14-15/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:14-15/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:14-15/r3.claim: Remembering the Lord's name means recalling that one will stand before him, beginning prayer with the takbir Allahu akbar.
ELMALILI:87:14-15/r3.anchor: Rabbinin ismini anıp O’nun huzûruna varacağını düşünerek “Allahu ekber” diye tekbir alıp

ELMALILI:87:14-15/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:14-15/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:14-15/r4.claim: Prayer includes the five daily prayers and, according to a transmitted report, especially the Eid prayer.
ELMALILI:87:14-15/r4.anchor: namaz kılan beş vakit namazı ve bâhusus vârid olan rivayete göre bayram namazını kılan kimseler

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:15:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:15:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:15:anmerkung/r1.claim: With God’s name as object, dhakara likely means invoke rather than remember; its pairing with prayer points to a publicly audible and visible act.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:15:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Ḏakara in Verbindung mit dem Namen Gottes als Objekt bedeutet, wie Ambros anmerkt (Dictionary, 104), vermutlich eher „anrufen“ als „gedenken“

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:15:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:15:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:15:anmerkung/r2.claim: Other calls to invoke God’s name specify morning and evening or call for devotion, at Q 76:25 and Q 73:8.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:15:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Vgl. noch 76:25, wo die Aufforderung, Gottes Namen anzurufen, mit genauen Zeitangaben

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r1.claim: The second stanza again addresses the messenger: he first praises God, perhaps with close followers, then speaks to a wider audience with an admonition that makes verse 6’s revelation public in purpose.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r1.anchor: Das zweite Gesätz beginnt wie das erste mit einem Aufruf an den Verkünder

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r4.claim: Verses 10–11 contrast good and bad responses to proclamation; verse 11 expands the bad response with a conventional warning of Hell, balanced by the promise to the good in verses 14–15.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r4.anchor: Auf den das zweite Gesätz einleitenden Aufruf folgt in V. 10.11 eine Antithese

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r5.claim: The passage forms a chiasm: the responses of good and bad in verses 10–11 correspond to their fates in verses 12–15, as in Q 92:5–11 and 14–21.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r5.anchor: Zusammen mit der an den Guten gerichteten Verheißung V. 14.15 ergibt sich eine chiastische Struktur

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r6.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r6.claim: The warning’s implied content includes fear of God, continued purification, invocation of God’s name, and prayer; verse 15 reprises verse 1’s call to recall the Creator’s favors.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r6.anchor: Erwähnt werden ständiges Bemühen um „Läuterung“ sowie Anrufung des Namens Gottes und Gebet

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r7.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r7.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r7.claim: Calls to the messenger can make a general appeal, with the messenger exemplary for each believer, as Robinson argues.

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r8.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r8.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r8.claim: Prayer likely means participation in an existing cult practice, linked with the newly introduced practice of glorifying and invoking God’s name.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r8.anchor: Mit der Aufforderung zur Verrichtung des „Gebets“ (ṣallā) ist dabei wohl

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r7.claim: Those who heed admonition, cleanse hearts of shirk, sin, and bad character, purify themselves through prayer and charity, and remember God attain salvation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r7.anchor: öğütlere kulak veren, kalplerini şirk, günah ve kötü ahlâkın kirlerinden temizleyen, namaz kılıp sadaka ve zekât vermek suretiyle nefsini arındıran kimselerin kurtuluşa erecekleri

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r9.speaker: Bazı müfessirlere
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r9.claim: Some exegetes understand salla as the five daily prayers, some as the festival prayer, and others as supplication in the lexical sense of salat.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r9.anchor: Bazı müfessirlere göre bundan maksat bilinen beş vakit namazdır; bazılarına göre bayram namazı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r10.claim: Because the five daily prayers were prescribed near the end of the Meccan period and this surah is early, the author prefers understanding salat as the daily worship practiced by the first Muslims following the Prophet.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r10.anchor: buradaki salât kavramını da beş vakit namaz olarak değil, ilk müslümanların Hz. Peygamber’in örnekliğinde yerine getirdikleri günlük ibadet olarak anlamak uygun olur

ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r1.claim: Remembering the Lord's name entails tongue and heart together; tongue-only speech with an heedless heart earns no reward and cannot ground success.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r1.anchor: اسم ربه بلسانه وقلبه لا باسانه مع غفلة القلب

ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r2.claim: Inner remembrance is unquestionably praiseworthy, but taking it alone as the specific meaning here departs from the apparent wording.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r2.anchor: والذكر القلبي باستحضار اسمه تعالى في القلب وإن كان ممدوحابلا شبهة إلا أن إرادته بخصوصه مما ذكر خلاف الظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r3.speaker: بعض
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r3.claim: Majmaʿ al-Bayān records from some interpreters that the verse means inwardly remembering God.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r3.anchor: وحكاه في مجمع البيان عن بعض

ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses remembrance as recalling one's return and standing before the Lord, an interpretation supported by the wording's inclusion of “name.”
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r4.anchor: وما روي عن ابن عباس من قوله أي ذكر معاده وموقفه بين يدي ربه عز وجل ظاهر فيه وفي إقحام لفظ اسم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r5.speaker: بعض الحنفية
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r5.claim: Some Ḥanafīs take the remembrance as the opening takbīr and the prayer as the five prescribed prayers; this is also transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās and in a raised report.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r5.anchor: وذهب بعض الحنفية إلى أن المراد بهذا الذكر تكبيرة الأفتتاح كأنه قيل وكبر للأفتتاح فصلى أي الصلوات الخمس

ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r6.claim: Other readings of prayer include the obligatory prayer together with whatever supererogatory prayers are possible.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r6.anchor: وقيل الصلاة المفروضة وما أمكن من النوافل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r7.claim: The opening-takbīr interpretation is used to argue that takbīr is obligatory, since success is attached to it and purification from shirk and prayer are obligations.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r7.anchor: واحتج بذلك على وجوب التكبيرة حيث نيط به الفلاح ووقع بن واجبين بل فرضين التزكي من الشرك والصلاة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r8.claim: Its proponents also say worship's precaution is obligatory and that the opening may be made with any divine name.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r8.anchor: مع أن الأحتياط في العبادات واجب فلا يضر الأحتمال وعلى أن الافتتاح جائز بكل اسم من أسمائه عز وجل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r9.claim: Al-Ālūsī finds the argument weak: fa-coordination can suggest takbīr is a condition rather than a pillar, and treating prayer as part of the remembrance needs an evident rhetorical purpose that is absent.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r9.anchor: والأنصاف أنه مع ما سمعت احتجاج ليس بالقوي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r10.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r10.claim: A further interpretation makes the remembrance specifically saying bismillah before prayer, which al-Ālūsī dismisses.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r10.anchor: وقيل هو خصوص بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم قبل الصلاة وليس بشيء

ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r11.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r11.claim: ʿAlī explains purification as the fitr alms, remembrance as the Eid takbīr, and prayer as Eid prayer; early authorities also appear to support this reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r11.anchor: وعن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه تزكى أي تصدق صدقة الفطر وذكر اسم ربه كبر يوم العيد فصلى صلاة العيد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r12.claim: Objections note that Qur'anic mention puts prayer before alms and that the sūrah is Meccan, before the Eid or fitr alms existed.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r12.anchor: وتعقب بأن الصلاة مقدمة على الزكاة في القرآن وإن السورة مكية ولم يكن حينئذ عيد ولا فطر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r13.claim: Replies say ordering in mention does not always dictate action; here the reversal could guide people to pay before Eid prayer, as transmitted reports say they did.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r13.anchor: ورد بأن ذلك إذا ذكرت بإسمها أما إذا ذكرت بفعل فتقديمها غير مطرد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r14.claim: The reply further notes that the sūrah's Meccan status is not unanimous, or that its ruling may have been revealed after the sūrah itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r14.anchor: وكون السورة مكية غير مجمع عليه وعلى القول بمكيتها الذي هو الأصح يكون ذلك مما تأخر حكمه عن نزوله

ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r15.claim: Al-Ālūsī proposes purification from shirk by inward faith, naming God as the testimony lā ilāha illā Allāh, and prayer as the prescribed prayer; an Ibn ʿAbbās report supports it.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r15.anchor: تزكى أي تطهر من الشرك بأن آمن بقلبه اذكر اسم ربه أي قال لا إله إلا الله فصلى أي الصلاة المفروضة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r16.claim: This sequence represents affirmation in the heart, confession on the tongue, and bodily practice; prayer can stand for worship generally because it is religion's pillar and the foremost bodily act.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r16.anchor: فيكون تزكى إشارة إلى التصديق بالجنان وذكر اسم ربه إلى النطق باللسان وصلى إلى العمل بالأركان

ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r17.speaker: عطاء
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r17.claim: A report from ʿAṭāʾ through Ibn ʿAbbās, and from Yazīd al-Naḥwī through ʿIkrima and al-Ḥasan, lists the earliest revealed passages and places this sūrah later in that sequence.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r17.anchor: عطاء عن ابن عباس ويزيد النحوي عن عكرمة والحسن بن أبي الحسن

ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r18.claim: Because the two testimonies lā ilāha illā Allāh and Muḥammad rasūl Allāh together constitute the required remembrance, the wording can naturally refer to God's name in that testimony.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r18.anchor: إن من رداف لا إله إلا الله محمد رسول الله وكان ذكر الله تعالى المطلوب هو مجموع الجملتين

ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r19.claim: Qad introduces the expected good news after the preceding warning about the one who avoids remembrance; the sentence may answer an implied question about the rememberer, characterized here by purification.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p109#2/r19.anchor: وكلمه قد لما أنه عند الإخبار بسوء حال المنجنب عن الذكر في الآخرة يتوقع السامع الأخبار بحسن حال المتذكر فيها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r5.claim: A reading links remembering God’s name and prayer with going out for the Eid prayer after giving charity; Ibn Masud prayed for the one who gives then prays.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r5.anchor: فكان ابن مسعود يقول: رحم الله امرءا تصدق ثم صلى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r6.claim: Nafiʿ reports that Ibn Umar checked whether charity had been given before going to the prayer ground, connecting the verses to charity and Eid prayer; Abu al-Aliya and Ibn Sirin hold this view.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r6.anchor: وروى نافع: كان ابن عمر إذا صلى الغداة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r7.claim: Some object that the surah is Meccan, before Eid or fitr charity existed; al-Baghawi replies that revelation can precede the ruling, as with the Prophet’s lawful entry into Mecca and the prophecy of Badr.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r7.anchor: يجوز أن يكون النزول سابقا على الحكم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r8.claim: Remembering God may mean the Eid takbirs and prayer the Eid prayer; another view takes ṣalla here to mean supplication.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r8.anchor: قيل: الذكر: تكبيرات العيد، والصلاة: صلاة العيد

BAYDAWI-FULL:87:13-18/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:13-18/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:13-18/r3.claim: Remembering God with heart and tongue and then praying echoes 20:14; ذكر may mean the opening takbīr instead.

BAYDAWI-FULL:87:13-18/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:13-18/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:13-18/r4.claim: Another interpretation takes تزكى as giving the fitr alms, remembering God as the Eid takbīr, and prayer as the Eid prayer.
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:13-18/r4.anchor: وقيل { تزكى } تصدق للفطر { وذكر اسم ربه } كبره يوم العيد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r6.claim: Remembering God's attributes of beneficence delights the inner self and appears outwardly in words; recalling the name also evokes its named referent.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r6.anchor: إذا ذكر الصفة سر بها فأفاض باطنه على ظاهره

BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r7.claim: Ritual prayer is the greatest bodily worship, as almsgiving is the greatest worship of wealth, and remembrance and prayer protect from vanity and its defects.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r7.anchor: الصلاة الشرعية لأنها أعظم الذكر , فهي أعظم عبادات البدن

BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r8.claim: The purification, remembrance, and prayer reprise the opening's divine traits: removing defects and acquiring perfections; this paired ellipsis links prayer with escape from the greatest fire.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r8.anchor: وكان متخلقا بما ذكر من أخلاق الله في أول السورة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r9.claim: The wording can include fitr almsgiving, Eid takbirs, and Eid prayer despite the sura being Meccan, since wording is general and revelation may precede a ruling.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r9.anchor: والآية صالحة لإرادة زكاة الفطر وتكبيرات العيد وصلاته

BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r10.speaker: الرازي في اللوامع
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r10.claim: Al-Razi says fitr almsgiving precedes Eid prayer; Ibn Masud recited this verse after saying may God show mercy to one who gives charity then prays.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r10.anchor: قال الرازي في اللوامع : وتقدم زكاة الفطر على صلاة العيد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r11.speaker: ابن مسعود
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r11.claim: Ibn Masud linked the verse to giving charity and then praying, although the sura is Meccan and the ruling came later.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r11.anchor: وكان ابن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه يقول : رحم الله أمرأ تصدق ثم صلى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r5.claim: Ibn Umar instructed Nafi to act similarly and said the verse was revealed about this practice.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r5.anchor: وزاد البغوي أن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما كان يأمر نافعا رضي الله عنه بنحو ما قال ابن مسعود

BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r6.speaker: النبي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r6.claim: Al-Bazzar reports from Awf ibn Malik that the Prophet ordered fitr almsgiving before Eid prayer and recited this verse; the chain's Kathir ibn Abd Allah was judged hasan by al-Tirmidhi but weakened by others.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r6.anchor: وروى البزار : ( عن عوف بن مالك الأشجعي رضي الله تعالى عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان يأمر بزكاة الفطر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r7.claim: The sura's Meccan date does not prevent a later ruling, as the verse about the sanctuary's inviolability preceded its effect at the conquest.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r7.anchor: السورة مكية , وظهر أثر الحل يوم الفتح

DURR-FULL:v8p484/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r4.claim: A weak-chain report says the Prophet ordered the fiṭra alms before Eid prayer and recited these verses; another wording identifies the verse with fiṭra.
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r4.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان يأمر بزكاة الفطر قبل أن يصلي صلاة العيد

DURR-FULL:v8p484/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r5.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r5.claim: The Prophet recited these verses and distributed the fiṭra alms before going to the Eid prayer ground.
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r5.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

DURR-FULL:v8p484/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r6.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r6.claim: He explains purification as giving fiṭra before setting out for Eid, and remembering God and praying as going out and performing the prayer.
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r6.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه {قد أفلح من تزكى} قال: أعطى صدقة الفطر قبل أن يخرج إلى العيد

DURR-FULL:v8p484/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r8.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r8.claim: Ibn ʿUmar would give fiṭra as he set out and recite the two verses.
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r8.anchor: أن عبد الله بن عمر كان يقدم صدقة الفطر حين يغدو ثم يغدو وهو يتلو

DURR-FULL:v8p484/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r9.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r9.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says these verses were revealed about giving fiṭra before the Eid prayer.
DURR-FULL:v8p484/r9.anchor: عن نافع عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنه قال: إنما أنزلت هذه الآية في إخراج صدقة الفطر قبل صلاة العيد

DURR-FULL:v8p485/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r1.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r1.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says the verses were revealed about fiṭra: one gives the alms, then prays.
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r1.anchor: عن أبي العالية رضي الله عنه في قوله: {قد أفلح من تزكى وذكر اسم ربه فصلى} قال: نزلت في صدقة الفطر

DURR-FULL:v8p485/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r2.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r2.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya checked whether a visitor had eaten and sent his zakāt; he says Medina considered no charity better than fiṭra and providing water.
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r2.anchor: عن أبي خلدة رضي الله عنه قال: دخلت على أبي العالية فقال لي إذا غدوت غدا إلى العيد فمر بي

DURR-FULL:v8p485/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r4.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r4.claim: Ibn Sīrīn says one pays fiṭra and then goes out to pray.
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r4.anchor: عن محمد بن سيرين رضي الله عنه في قوله: {قد أفلح من تزكى} قال: أدى صدقة الفطر ثم خرج فصلى

DURR-FULL:v8p485/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r5.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r5.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī urges paying the zakāt as early as possible on Eid and cites these verses.
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r5.anchor: عن إبراهيم النخعي رضي الله عنه قال: قدم الزكاة ما استطعت يوم الفطر ثم قرأ

DURR-FULL:v8p485/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r9.speaker: أبو الأحوص
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r9.claim: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ urges anyone able to give charity before prayer to do so, citing the verse; another wording suggests praying two units after giving.
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r9.anchor: عن أبي الأحوص رضي الله عنه قال: رحم الله امرأ تصدق ثم صلى ثم قرأ {قد أفلح من تزكى}

DURR-FULL:v8p485/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r10.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says a person setting out for prayer may give charity, citing these verses.
DURR-FULL:v8p485/r10.anchor: أبي الأحوص عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال: إذا خرج أحدكم يريد الصلاة فلا عليه أن يتصدق بشيء

DURR-FULL:v8p488/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r6.claim: Asked whether the Prophet received anything from those scrolls, he recited the passage from purification and prayer through the superiority of the afterlife and the scrolls.
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r6.anchor: هل أنزل عليك شيء مما كان في صحف إبراهيم وموسى قال: يا أبا ذر نعم {قد أفلح من تزكى

TAB:87:15/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:15/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:87:15/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets remembering the Lord and praying as affirming His oneness.
TAB:87:15/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس وَذَكَرَ اسْمَ رَبّهِ فَصَلّى يقول : وحّد الله سبحانه وتعالى

TAB:87:15/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:15/r2.speaker: آخرون
TAB:87:15/r2.claim: Others interpret remembering the Lord as invoking Him and earnestly seeking Him.
TAB:87:15/r2.anchor: وقال آخرون : بل معنى ذلك : وذكر الله ودعاه ورغب إليه

TAB:87:15/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:15/r3.speaker: author
TAB:87:15/r3.claim: Al-Tabari includes both affirming God’s oneness and invoking and earnestly seeking Him, since the verse does not restrict remembrance to one kind.
TAB:87:15/r3.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك : أن يقال : وذكر الله فوحّده ، ودعاه ورغب إليه ، لأن كلّ ذلك من ذكر الله

TAB:87:15/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:15/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:87:15/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the prayer meant is the five daily prayers.
TAB:87:15/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، قوله : فَصَلّىيقول : صّلى الصلوات الخمس

TAB:87:15/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:15/r5.speaker: آخرون
TAB:87:15/r5.claim: Another interpretation identifies the prayer as the Eid prayer on the day of breaking the fast.
TAB:87:15/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون : عني به : صلاة العيد يوم الفطر

TAB:87:15/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:15/r6.speaker: آخرون
TAB:87:15/r6.claim: Others take prayer here to mean supplication.
TAB:87:15/r6.anchor: وقال آخرون : بل عُني به : وذكر اسم ربه فدعا وقالوا : الصلاة ها هنا : الدعاء

TAB:87:15/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:15/r7.speaker: author
TAB:87:15/r7.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the ritual prayers, in which one remembers God through praise, glorification, and supplication.
TAB:87:15/r7.anchor: والصواب من القول أن يقال : عُنِي بقوله : فَصَلّى : الصلوات ، وذكر الله فيها بالتحميد والتمجيد والدعاء

ITQAN:v1p106/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p106/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
ITQAN:v1p106/r1.claim: Ibn Umar reports that the verse was revealed about the alms of breaking the fast; al-Bazzar gives a similar report raised to the Prophet.
ITQAN:v1p106/r1.anchor: فقد روى البيهقي وغيره عن ابن عمر أنها نزلت في زكاة الفطر وأخرج البزار نحوه مرفوعا

ITQAN:v1p106/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p106/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ITQAN:v1p106/r2.claim: Some object that the interpretation cannot fit a Meccan surah because Mecca had no Eid, zakat, or fasting.
ITQAN:v1p106/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم لا أدري ما وجه هذا التأويل لأن السورة مكية ولم يكن بمكة عيد ولا زكاة ولا صوم

ITQAN:v1p106/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p106/r3.speaker: البغوي
ITQAN:v1p106/r3.claim: Al-Baghawi answers that revelation can precede a legal ruling, as al-Balad anticipated the special permission that took effect at the conquest of Mecca.
ITQAN:v1p106/r3.anchor: وأجاب البغوي بأنه يجوز أن يكون النزول سابقا على الحكم كما قال ﴿ لا أقسم بهذا البلد وأنت حل بهذا البلد ﴾

ITQAN:v1p106/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p106/r8.speaker: ابن الحصار
ITQAN:v1p106/r8.claim: Ibn al-Hassar says Meccan surahs often mention zakat in anticipation of the religion’s establishment; zakat itself was collected only in Medina, by consensus.
ITQAN:v1p106/r8.anchor: وقال ابن الحصار ذكر الله الزكاة في السور المكيات كثيرا تصريحا وتعريضا بأن الله سينجز وعده لرسوله

ITQAN:v2p338#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p338#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p338#2/r1.claim: Suyuti glosses “purifies himself” as being free of polytheism.

ITQAN:v2p338#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p338#2/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p338#2/r2.claim: “He remembers his Lord’s name” means that he affirms God’s oneness.

ITQAN:v2p338#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p338#2/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p338#2/r3.claim: “Then he prayed” means that he performed the five prayers.

ITQAN:v4p535#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p535#3/r1.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
ITQAN:v4p535#3/r1.claim: Jabir reports the Prophet’s gloss: purification is testifying to God’s oneness, rejecting idols, and testifying to his messengership; remembering God and praying refers to keeping up the five prayers.
ITQAN:v4p535#3/r1.anchor: أخرج البزار عن جابر بن عبد الله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ﴿ قد أفلح من تزكى ﴾ ( من شهد أن لا إله إلا الله وخلع الأنداد

NASHR:v2p112/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p112/r6.speaker: أصحاب التفريق بين رؤوس الآي وغيرها
NASHR:v2p112/r6.claim: Some soften lām at verse endings for euphony and emphatically pronounce it elsewhere because of the preceding trigger; Ibn al-Jazari cites this as a preferred distinction.
NASHR:v2p112/r6.anchor: فرققوها في رءوس الآي للتناسب وغلظوها في غيرها لوجود الموجب قبلها

NASHR:v2p112/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p112/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p112/r7.claim: The verse-final examples are fa-la saddaqa wa-la salla, wa-dhakara isma rabbihi fa-salla, and idha salla; non-final examples include yasla al-nar.
NASHR:v2p112/r7.anchor: فلا صدق ولا صلى في القيامة وذكر اسم ربه فصلى في سبح إذا صلى في العلق

ABUHAYYAN:87:15/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:15/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:87:15/r1.claim: Remembering the Lord’s name means affirming His oneness without associating partners; prayer includes obligatory prayer and whatever voluntary prayers one can perform.
ABUHAYYAN:87:15/r1.anchor: { وذكر اسم ربه } : أي وحده ، لم يقرنه بشيء من الأنداد ، { فصلى } : أي أتى الصلاة المفروضة وما أمكنه من النوافل

ABUHAYYAN:87:15/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:15/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:87:15/r2.claim: The meaning is that remembering God leads to belief; the verse says the successful person performs both worship and charity.
ABUHAYYAN:87:15/r2.anchor: والمعنى : أنه لما تذكر آمن بالله ، ثم أخبر عنه تعالى أنه أفلح من أتى بهاتين العبادتين الصلاة والزكاة

ABUHAYYAN:87:15/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:15/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:87:15/r3.claim: An argument that the verse requires the opening takbīr, permits any divine name for it, and places it outside prayer is weak.
ABUHAYYAN:87:15/r3.anchor: لأن الصلاة معطوفة على الذكر الذي هو تكبيرة الافتتاح ، وهو احتجاج ضعيف .

ABUHAYYAN:87:15/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:15/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN:87:15/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says remembering the Lord means remembering the return and standing before Him; then the person prays to Him.
ABUHAYYAN:87:15/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : { وذكر اسم ربه } : أي معاده وموقفه بين يدي ربه ، { فصلى له }

ALUSI:87:15/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:15/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:15/r1.claim: Remembrance of the Lord is with both tongue and heart; heedless verbal mention earns no reward and should not be what success depends on.
ALUSI:87:15/r1.anchor: بلسانه وقلبه لا بلسانه مع غفلة القلب إذ مثل ذلك لا ثواب فيه

ALUSI:87:15/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:15/r2.speaker: بعض
ALUSI:87:15/r2.claim: A view cited in Majmaʿ al-Bayān takes remembrance as recalling God's name inwardly; al-Ālūsī says that exclusive sense departs from the apparent wording.
ALUSI:87:15/r2.anchor: خلاف الظاهر وحكاه في «مجمع البيان » عن بعض

ALUSI:87:15/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:15/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI:87:15/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the person remembered his return and standing before his Lord; al-Ālūsī finds this apparent in the gloss.
ALUSI:87:15/r3.anchor: وما روى عن ابن عباس من قوله أي ذكر معاده وموقفه بين يدي ربه عز وجل

ALUSI:87:15/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:15/r4.speaker: بعض الحنفية
ALUSI:87:15/r4.claim: Some Hanafis identify remembrance of the Lord's name with the opening takbīr, effectively reading it as saying the takbīr to begin prayer.
ALUSI:87:15/r4.anchor: وذهب بعض الحنفية إلى أن المراد بهذا الذكر تكبيرة الافتتاح

ALUSI:87:15/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:15/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI:87:15/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses prayer as the five daily prayers; al-Ālūsī adds that this was also related in a raised Prophetic hadith.
ALUSI:87:15/r5.anchor: أي الصلوات الخمس كما أخرجه ابن المنذر وغيره عن ابن عباس

ALUSI:87:15/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:15/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:87:15/r6.claim: Another interpretation makes it obligatory prayer together with whatever supererogatory prayers are possible.
ALUSI:87:15/r6.anchor: وقيل الصلاة المفروضة وما أمكن من النوافل

ALUSI:87:15/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:15/r7.speaker: بعض الحنفية
ALUSI:87:15/r7.claim: The opening-takbīr interpretation is used to argue its obligation, since success is tied to it and it falls between purification from shirk and prayer, both obligatory.
ALUSI:87:15/r7.anchor: واحتج بذلك على وجوب التكبيرة حيث نيط به الفلاح ووقع بين واجبين بل فرضين

ALUSI:87:15/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:15/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:15/r8.claim: On the opening-takbīr reading, the general wording apparently permits beginning prayer with any of God's names.
ALUSI:87:15/r8.anchor: وعلى أن الافتتاح جائز بكل اسم من أسمائه عز وجل وهو ظاهر

ALUSI:87:15/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:15/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:15/r9.claim: The claim that takbīr is a condition rather than a pillar relies on faʾ; treating prayer as a whole after its part or a general after a particular needs an otherwise unshown rhetorical purpose.
ALUSI:87:15/r9.anchor: وعلى أن التكبيرة شرط لا ركن للعطف بالفاء وعطف الكل على الجزء

ALUSI:87:15/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:15/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:15/r10.claim: Al-Ālūsī judges the proof for making takbīr a pillar weak, since the proposed whole-part reading lacks a demonstrated rhetorical point.
ALUSI:87:15/r10.anchor: والإنصاف أنه مع ما سمعت احتجاج ليس بالقوي

ALUSI:87:15/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:15/r11.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:87:15/r11.claim: A further view identifies remembrance with reciting the basmala before prayer; al-Ālūsī dismisses it.
ALUSI:87:15/r11.anchor: وقيل هو خصوص بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم قبل الصلاة وليس بشيء

ALUSI:87:15/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:15/r12.speaker: علي
ALUSI:87:15/r12.claim: ʿAlī glosses purification as paying fitra, remembrance as the Eid takbīr, and prayer as the Eid prayer.
ALUSI:87:15/r12.anchor: أي تصدق صدقة الفطر وذكر اسم ربه كبر يوم العيد فصلى صلاة العيد

ALUSI:87:15/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:15/r13.speaker: جماعة من السلف
ALUSI:87:15/r13.claim: Al-Ālūsī says reports from a group of early authorities appear to support the Eid and fitra interpretation.
ALUSI:87:15/r13.anchor: وعن جماعة من السلف ما يقتضي ظاهره ذلك

ALUSI:87:15/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:15/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:15/r14.claim: Objections are that prayer precedes zakāt in Qurʾānic ordering and the sūra is Meccan, when there was no Eid or fitra; replies note verbal order is not fixed, cite 75:31, and say the unusual order may urge paying fitra before Eid prayer, as reports describe.
ALUSI:87:15/r14.anchor: إذا ذكرت بفعل فتقديمها غير مطرد

ALUSI:87:15/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:15/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:15/r15.claim: Meccan provenance is not unanimously accepted; if the stronger Meccan view is right, the ruling may have taken effect after the sūra's revelation.
ALUSI:87:15/r15.anchor: وكون السورة مكية غير مجمع عليه وعلى القول بمكيتها الذي هو الأصح

ALUSI:87:15/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:15/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:15/r16.claim: Al-Ālūsī allows purification to mean cleansing from shirk through inward faith, remembrance to mean uttering the testimony that there is no god but God, and prayer to mean obligatory prayer.
ALUSI:87:15/r16.anchor: وأقول يجوز أن يقال تزكى أي تطهر من الشرك بأن آمن من بقلبه

ALUSI:87:15/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:15/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:15/r17.claim: This maps purification to assent of the heart, remembrance to the tongue, and prayer to bodily action; prayer is the religion's pillar, best bodily deed, and restrains indecency, so it can represent embodied duties and worship.
ALUSI:87:15/r17.anchor: فيكون تزكى إشارة إلى التصديق بالجنان وذكر اسم ربه إلى النطق باللسان

ALUSI:87:15/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:15/r18.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:87:15/r18.claim: Prayer may be singled out because bodily obligations were not yet fully established when the sūra descended, and prayer was the most important revealed duty if any others had been revealed.
ALUSI:87:15/r18.anchor: وقد يقال اقتصر على ذكر الصلاة لأن الفرائض والواجبات البدنية لم تكن تامة يوم نزول السورة

ALUSI:87:15/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:15/r19.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس ويزيد النحوي عن عكرمة والحسن
ALUSI:87:15/r19.claim: A report orders early revelations as al-ʿAlaq, Nūn, al-Muzzammil, al-Muddaththir, al-Masad, al-Takwīr, then this sūra's opening; it contextualizes prayer's early importance.
ALUSI:87:15/r19.anchor: وقد روى عطاء عن ابن عباس ويزيد النحوي عن عكرمة والحسن

ALUSI:87:15/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:15/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:15/r20.claim: If the testimony that Muḥammad is God's messenger is paired with divine unity, the required remembrance may encompass both clauses, making this reading plausible.
ALUSI:87:15/r20.anchor: إن من رادف لا إله إلا الله محمد رسول الله وكان ذكر الله تعالى المطلوب هو مجموع الجملتين

BAGHAWI:87:15/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:15/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
BAGHAWI:87:15/r1.claim: Ibn Masud prayed that God show mercy to whoever gives charity and then prays, and recited this verse.
BAGHAWI:87:15/r1.anchor: رحم الله امرأً تصدق ثم صلى ،   ثم يقرأ هذه الآية

BAGHAWI:87:15/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:15/r2.speaker: نافع
BAGHAWI:87:15/r2.claim: Nafi reports that Ibn Umar checked after the Eid morning prayer whether the fitr charity had been given; if not, he ordered it given before going to the prayer ground.
BAGHAWI:87:15/r2.anchor: يا نافع أخرجت الصدقة ؟ فإن قلت : نعم ،   مضى إلى المصلى

BAGHAWI:87:15/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:15/r3.speaker: أبو العالية وابن سيرين
BAGHAWI:87:15/r3.claim: They take the passage to refer to giving zakat al-fitr and performing the Eid prayer.
BAGHAWI:87:15/r3.anchor: قد أفلح من تزكى * وذكر اسم ربه فصلى } وهو قول أبي العالية وابن سيرين

BAGHAWI:87:15/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:15/r4.speaker: بعضهم
BAGHAWI:87:15/r4.claim: An unnamed critic questions this interpretation because the sura is Meccan, when there was neither Eid nor fitr charity in Mecca.
BAGHAWI:87:15/r4.anchor: لأن هذه السورة مكية ،   ولم يكن بمكة عيد ولا زكاة فطر

BAGHAWI:87:15/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:15/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:87:15/r5.claim: Baghawi answers that revelation may precede the legal ruling, as with the Meccan verses about Muhammad being permitted in Mecca and the defeat of the enemy host, fulfilled later at the conquest and Badr.
BAGHAWI:87:15/r5.anchor: يجوز أن يكون النزول سابقاً على الحكم كما قال : { وأنت حل بهذا البلد }

BAGHAWI:87:15/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:15/r6.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
BAGHAWI:87:15/r6.claim: Umar says he did not know which host would be defeated until Badr, when he saw the Prophet recite the prediction while standing in his armor.
