BAGHAWI:87:15/r6.anchor: كنت لا أدري أي جمع يهزم ،   فلما كان يوم بدر رأيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يثبت في الدرع

BAGHAWI:87:15/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:15/r7.speaker: بعضهم
BAGHAWI:87:15/r7.claim: One interpretation takes remembrance as the Eid takbirs and prayer as the Eid prayer.
BAGHAWI:87:15/r7.anchor: قيل : الذكر : تكبيرات العيد ،   والصلاة : صلاة العيد

BAGHAWI:87:15/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:15/r8.speaker: بعضهم
BAGHAWI:87:15/r8.claim: Another interpretation takes the prayer here to mean supplication.
BAGHAWI:87:15/r8.anchor: والصلاة : صلاة العيد ،   وقيل : الصلاة ها هنا الدعاء

BAYDAWI:87:15/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:87:15/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:87:15/r1.claim: Remembrance with heart and tongue followed by prayer echoes 20:14.
BAYDAWI:87:15/r1.anchor: وذكر اسم ربه بقلبه ولسانه فصلى كقوله وأقم الصلاة لذكري

BAYDAWI:87:15/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:87:15/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:87:15/r2.claim: Another view takes remembrance of the Lord's name as the opening takbīr.

BAYDAWI:87:15/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:87:15/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:87:15/r3.claim: A ritual interpretation links purification to alms at the end of Ramadan, remembrance to the Eid takbīr, and prayer to the Eid prayer.
BAYDAWI:87:15/r3.anchor: وقيل تزكى تصدق للفطر وذكر اسم ربه كبره يوم العيد فصلى صلاته

BIQAI:87:15/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:15/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:15/r1.claim: Remembrance and prayer are the greatest purifying deeds.
BIQAI:87:15/r1.anchor: ولما كان أعظم الأعمال المزكية الذكر والصلاة قال تعالى

BIQAI:87:15/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:15/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:15/r2.claim: The noun for remembrance occurs with either kasra or ḍamma on its initial consonant.
BIQAI:87:15/r2.anchor: أي بالقلب واللسان ذكر وذكر - بالكسر والضم

BIQAI:87:15/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:15/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:15/r3.claim: God's name refers to His beneficent attributes: recalling an attribute delights the heart and brings it to the tongue, while uttering the name inscribes its bearer in the heart.
BIQAI:87:15/r3.anchor: إذا ذكر الصفة سر بها فأفاض باطنه على ظاهره

BIQAI:87:15/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:15/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:15/r4.claim: Prayer means the prescribed ritual prayer, the greatest bodily worship, just as zakāt is the greatest worship of wealth; it is itself the greatest remembrance.
BIQAI:87:15/r4.anchor: أي الصلاة الشرعية لأنها أعظم الذكر ، فهي أعظم عبادات البدن

BIQAI:87:15/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:15/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:15/r5.claim: Purification, remembrance, and prayer remove self-admiration and its faults, strip away defects, and acquire perfections modeled on the sūra's opening; the passage also evokes stages of medical treatment.
BIQAI:87:15/r5.anchor: وكان متخلقاً بما ذكر من أخلاق الله في أول السورة من التخلي عن النقائص بالتزكية

BIQAI:87:15/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:15/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:15/r6.claim: Only someone persistent in remembering God's name is fit to remember Him; such a person escapes misery and the great fire, as God has promised without fail.
BIQAI:87:15/r6.anchor: فلا يشقى فلا يصلى النار الكبرى بوعد لا خلف فيه

BIQAI:87:15/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:15/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:15/r7.claim: A second interwoven omission links the fire mentioned first with its omitted opposite in the next verse, and the purification named next with its omitted opposite earlier; purification, remembrance, and prayer figure in a therapy sequence.
BIQAI:87:15/r7.anchor: من الاحتباك في الاحتباك : ذكر أولاً الصلى دليلاً على حذف

BIQAI:87:15/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:15/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:15/r8.claim: The general wording can include zakāt al-fiṭr, the Eid takbīrs, and Eid prayer even though the sūra is Meccan and fasting was prescribed in Medina; revelation may precede a ruling.
BIQAI:87:15/r8.anchor: والآية صالحة لإرادة زكاة الفطر وتكبيرات العيد وصلاته وإن كانت السورة مكية

BIQAI:87:15/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:15/r9.speaker: الرازي
BIQAI:87:15/r9.claim: Al-Rāzī in al-Lawāmiʿ says zakāt al-fiṭr precedes Eid prayer and cites Ibn Masʿūd's prayer for the giver of charity before reciting this verse.
BIQAI:87:15/r9.anchor: قال الرازي في اللوامع : وتقدم زكاة الفطر على صلاة العيد

BIQAI:87:15/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:15/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود
BIQAI:87:15/r10.claim: Ibn Masʿūd prayed for mercy on whoever gave charity and then prayed, and then recited this verse.
BIQAI:87:15/r10.anchor: ابن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه يقول : رحم الله امرأً تصدق ثم صلى

BIQAI:87:15/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:15/r11.speaker: ابن عمر
BIQAI:87:15/r11.claim: Al-Baghawī reports that Ibn ʿUmar told Nāfiʿ to do likewise and said the verse was revealed concerning this practice.
BIQAI:87:15/r11.anchor: أن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما كان يأمر نافعاً رضي الله عنه بنحو ما قال ابن مسعود

BIQAI:87:15/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:15/r12.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI:87:15/r12.claim: Al-Bazzār reports from ʿAwf ibn Mālik al-Ashjaʿī that the Prophet ordered zakāt al-fiṭr before Eid prayer and recited this verse.
BIQAI:87:15/r12.anchor: عن عوف بن مالك الأشجعي رضي الله تعالى عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان يأمر بزكاة الفطر قبل أن يصلي صلاة العيد

BIQAI:87:15/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:15/r13.speaker: الترمذي
BIQAI:87:15/r13.claim: The report's chain includes Kathīr ibn ʿAbd Allāh, whom al-Tirmidhī graded ḥasan while other critics weakened him.
BIQAI:87:15/r13.anchor: وفي السند كثير بن عبد الله - حسّن له الترمذي وضعفه غيره

BIQAI:87:15/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:15/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:15/r14.claim: The source invokes the Meccan verse about the Prophet being permitted in this town as precedent for a revelation preceding its later legal realization at the conquest.
BIQAI:87:15/r14.anchor: والسورة مكية ، وظهر أثر الحل يوم الفتح

DURR:87:14/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:87:14/r1.claim: Jābir reports the Prophet explaining purification as affirming God’s oneness, rejecting idols, and testifying to his messengership; remembrance and prayer mean five prayers observed carefully and on time.
DURR:87:14/r1.anchor: عن جابر بن عبدالله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR:87:14/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:87:14/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses purification as freedom from shirk, remembrance as affirming God’s oneness, and prayer as five daily prayers.
DURR:87:14/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله

DURR:87:14/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:87:14/r8.claim: A weak report says the Prophet ordered fiṭr charity before Eid prayer and recited these verses; another wording identifies the verse as fiṭr charity.
DURR:87:14/r8.anchor: بسند ضعيف عن كثير بن عبدالله بن عمرو بن عوف عن أبيه عن جده عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان يأمر بزكاة الفطر قبل أن يصلي صلاة العيد

DURR:87:14/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:87:14/r9.claim: Abū Saʿīd reports the Prophet recited the verses and distributed fiṭr charity before Eid prayer.
DURR:87:14/r9.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه

DURR:87:14/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r10.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
DURR:87:14/r10.claim: Abū Saʿīd interprets purification as paying fiṭr charity before Eid; remembrance and prayer mean going out to Eid and praying.
DURR:87:14/r10.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه { قد أفلح من تزكى } قال : أعطى صدقة الفطر قبل أن يخرج إلى العيد

DURR:87:14/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r12.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
DURR:87:14/r12.claim: Qatāda reports that ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUmar paid fiṭr charity before Eid, reciting the verses.
DURR:87:14/r12.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه أن عبدالله بن عمر كان يقدم صدقة الفطر حين يغدو ثم يغدو وهو يتلو { قد أفلح من تزكى

DURR:87:14/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r13.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR:87:14/r13.claim: Nāfiʿ reports Ibn ʿUmar’s view that these verses were revealed about paying fiṭr charity before Eid prayer.
DURR:87:14/r13.anchor: عن نافع عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنه قال : إنما أنزلت هذه الآية في إخراج صدقة الفطر قبل صلاة العيد

DURR:87:14/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r15.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR:87:14/r15.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says the verses were revealed about fiṭr charity: purify, then pray.
DURR:87:14/r15.anchor: عن أبي العالية رضي الله عنه

DURR:87:14/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r16.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR:87:14/r16.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya asked a visitor before Eid whether he had eaten and sent charity; he cited the verses and praised fiṭr charity and providing water.
DURR:87:14/r16.anchor: عن أبي خلدة رضي الله عنه قال : دخلت على أبي العالية

DURR:87:14/r18.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r18.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
DURR:87:14/r18.claim: Muḥammad b. Sīrīn says the person paid fiṭr charity, then went out and prayed.
DURR:87:14/r18.anchor: عن محمد بن سيرين رضي الله عنه

DURR:87:14/r19.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r19.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
DURR:87:14/r19.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī advised paying charity as early as possible on Eid, citing the verses.
DURR:87:14/r19.anchor: عن إبراهيم النخعي رضي الله عنه قال : قدم الزكاة ما استطعت يوم الفطر ثم قرأ { قد أفلح من تزكى وذكر اسم ربه فصلى }

DURR:87:14/r24.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r24.speaker: أبو الأحوص
DURR:87:14/r24.claim: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ urged charity before prayer; one wording says do so if able, another says give, pray, and recite the verse.
DURR:87:14/r24.anchor: عن أبي الأحوص رضي الله عنه قال : رحم الله امرئ تصدق ثم صلى ثم قرأ { قد أفلح من تزكى } الآية

DURR:87:14/r25.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r25.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR:87:14/r25.claim: Through Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, Ibn Masʿūd says one setting out for prayer may give charity, citing the verses.
DURR:87:14/r25.anchor: من طريق أبي الأحوص عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال : إذا خرج أحدكم يريد الصلاة فلا عليه أن يتصدق بشيء

DURR:87:14/r26.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:14/r26.speaker: أبو الأحوص
DURR:87:14/r26.claim: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ also says a donor should pray two rakʿas and recite the verse.
DURR:87:14/r26.anchor: عن أبي الأحوص رضي الله عنه قال : لو أن الذي تصدق بالصدقة صلى ركعتين ثم قرأ { قد أفلح من تزكى } الآية

DURR:87:15/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r1.speaker: النبي
DURR:87:15/r1.claim: Jabir reports the Prophet glossing purification as affirming God's oneness, renouncing idols, and testifying to his messengerhood; remembrance and prayer mean the five prayers kept at their times.
DURR:87:15/r1.anchor: عن جابر بن عبدالله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR:87:15/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:87:15/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses purification as freedom from shirk, remembrance as affirming God's oneness, and prayer as the five daily prayers.
DURR:87:15/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

DURR:87:15/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r7.speaker: النبي
DURR:87:15/r7.claim: A report through Kathir ibn Abd Allah, whose chain al-Suyuti calls weak, says the Prophet directed fitr alms before Eid prayer and recited these verses; another wording identifies purification as fitr alms.
DURR:87:15/r7.anchor: بسند ضعيف عن كثير بن عبدالله بن عمرو بن عوف عن أبيه عن جده عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR:87:15/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r8.speaker: النبي
DURR:87:15/r8.claim: Abu Sa'id reports that the Prophet recited these verses and distributed fitr alms before setting out for the Eid prayer ground.
DURR:87:15/r8.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه

DURR:87:15/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r9.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
DURR:87:15/r9.claim: Abu Sa'id interprets purification as paying fitr alms before leaving for Eid and the following phrase as going out to pray.
DURR:87:15/r9.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه

DURR:87:15/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r10.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR:87:15/r10.claim: Qatada reports that Ibn Umar would pay fitr alms when departing in the morning, then leave while reciting these verses.
DURR:87:15/r10.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه أن عبدالله بن عمر كان يقدم صدقة الفطر

DURR:87:15/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r11.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR:87:15/r11.claim: Ibn Umar says the verses were revealed concerning payment of fitr alms before the Eid prayer.
DURR:87:15/r11.anchor: عن نافع عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنه

DURR:87:15/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r13.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR:87:15/r13.claim: Abu al-Aliya says the verses were revealed about fitr alms: purify first, then pray.
DURR:87:15/r13.anchor: عن أبي العالية رضي الله عنه في قوله

DURR:87:15/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r14.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR:87:15/r14.claim: Abu Khilda recounts that Abu al-Aliya asked whether he had paid his alms before Eid, then said Medinans knew no better charity than fitr alms and providing water.
DURR:87:15/r14.anchor: عن أبي خلدة رضي الله عنه

DURR:87:15/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r16.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
DURR:87:15/r16.claim: Ibn Sirin says the successful person pays fitr alms, then goes out and prays.
DURR:87:15/r16.anchor: عن محمد بن سيرين رضي الله عنه في قوله

DURR:87:15/r17.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r17.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
DURR:87:15/r17.claim: Al-Nakha'i advises paying the fitr alms as early as possible on Eid, then cites the verses.
DURR:87:15/r17.anchor: عن إبراهيم النخعي رضي الله عنه

DURR:87:15/r22.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r22.speaker: أبو الأحوص
DURR:87:15/r22.claim: Abu al-Ahwas urges giving charity before praying, citing the verse; one wording says whoever can give charity before prayer should do so.
DURR:87:15/r22.anchor: عن أبي الأحوص رضي الله عنه

DURR:87:15/r23.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r23.speaker: أبو الأحوص
DURR:87:15/r23.claim: Abu al-Ahwas says a person who gives charity should pray two cycles and then recite the verse.
DURR:87:15/r23.anchor: عن أبي الأحوص رضي الله عنه

DURR:87:15/r24.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:15/r24.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR:87:15/r24.claim: Abu al-Ahwas transmits Ibn Mas'ud's view that one leaving for prayer may give some charity, based on these verses.
DURR:87:15/r24.anchor: أبي الأحوص عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه

IBNASHUR:87:1/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:1/r8.speaker: ابن عمر وابن عباس
IBNASHUR:87:1/r8.claim: Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas say verses 14–15 came down about Eid prayer and alms at the end of Ramadan, making those verses Medinan and the sura partly Makkan and partly Medinan.
IBNASHUR:87:1/r8.anchor: وعن ابن عمر وابن عباس أن قوله تعالى { قد أفلح من تزكى وذكر اسم ربه فصلى } نزل في صلاة العيد وصدقة الفطر

IBNASHUR:87:14/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:14/r10.speaker: ابن عباس وعطاء وعكرمة وقتادة
IBNASHUR:87:14/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ata, Ikrimah, and Qatadah identify remembering God’s name and praying with the five daily prayers and careful observance of them.
IBNASHUR:87:14/r10.anchor: قال : هي الصلوات الخمس والمحافظة عليها والاهتمام بها ، وهو قول ابن عباس وعطاء وعكرمة وقتادة

IBNASHUR:87:15/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:15/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:15/r1.claim: Remembering God’s name may mean verbal remembrance, naming God with reverence through phrases such as There is no god but God, God is greatest, and Glory be to God; compare verse 1.
IBNASHUR:87:15/r1.anchor: وفعل { ذكر اسم ربه } يجوز أن يكون من الذكر اللساني الذي هو بكسر الذال

IBNASHUR:87:15/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:15/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:15/r2.claim: Alternatively, remembrance may mean inward awareness; name is then an inserted expression pointing to God’s affairs and perfect attributes.
IBNASHUR:87:15/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون من الذكر بضم الذال وهو حضور الشيء في النفس الذاكرة والمفكرة

IBNASHUR:87:15/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:15/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:15/r3.claim: On either reading of remembrance, it leads naturally to prayer as humility before God, praise, and drawing near to Him.
IBNASHUR:87:15/r3.anchor: وتفريع { فصلى } على { ذكر اسم ربه } على كلا الوجهين لأن الذكر بمعنييه يبعث الذاكر على تعظيم الله تعالى

IBNASHUR:87:15/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:15/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:15/r4.claim: The three qualities follow their natural order: remove false beliefs and corrupt thoughts, know God’s perfect qualities and wisdom so as to fear and hope, then turn to obedience and worship.
IBNASHUR:87:15/r4.anchor: وقد رتبت هذه الخصال الثلاث على الآية على ترتيب تولدها . فأصلها : إزالة الخباثة النفسية من عقائد باطلة

IBNASHUR:87:15/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:15/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:15/r5.claim: Prayer represents worship more broadly; as obedience itself, it is followed by the other prescribed deeds.
IBNASHUR:87:15/r5.anchor: والصلاة تشير إلى العبادة وهي في ذاتها طاعة وامتثال يأتي بعده ما يشرع من الأعمال

IBNASHUR:87:15/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:15/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:15/r6.claim: The relation between prayer and remembrance is supported by 29:45, which says prayer restrains indecency and wrongdoing while remembrance of God is greater.
IBNASHUR:87:15/r6.anchor: قال تعالى : { إن الصلاة تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر ولذكر الله أكبر } [ العنكبوت : 45 ]

IBNATIYYA:87:15/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:15/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:87:15/r1.claim: Remembering the Lord's name means affirming His oneness; prayer includes obligatory prayers and whatever voluntary prayer and good works one can manage.
IBNATIYYA:87:15/r1.anchor: وقوله { وذكر اسم ربه } معناه : وحده وصلى له الصلوات التي فرضت عليه ، وتنفل أيضا بما أمكنه من صلاة وبر

IBNATIYYA:87:15/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:15/r2.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري وابن عمر وابن المسيب
IBNATIYYA:87:15/r2.claim: They apply the verses to Eid al-Fitr: giving zakat al-fitr, remembering God on the way to the prayer ground until the imam appears, and performing the Eid prayer.
IBNATIYYA:87:15/r2.anchor: وقال أبو سعيد الخدري وابن عمر وابن المسيب : هذه الآية في صبيحة يوم الفطر فتزكى ، أدى زكاة الفطر

IBNATIYYA:87:15/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:15/r3.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
IBNATIYYA:87:15/r3.claim: A report from Abu Sa'id says the Prophet recited this verse and distributed the fitra before setting out for the Eid prayer.
IBNATIYYA:87:15/r3.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

IBNATIYYA:87:15/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:15/r4.speaker: قتادة وكثير من المتأولين
IBNATIYYA:87:15/r4.claim: Qatada and many interpreters take tazakkā as paying wealth-zakat and ṣallā as performing the five daily prayers.
IBNATIYYA:87:15/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة وكثير من المتأولين : { تزكى } : أدى زكاة ماله ، و «صلى » معناه صلى الخمس

IBNKATHIR:87:15/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r1.claim: Remembering God and praying means establishing prayer at its appointed times to seek His pleasure, obey Him, and follow His law.
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r1.anchor: أي : أقام الصلاة في أوقاتها ؛ ابتغاء رضوان الله وطاعة لأمر الله وامتثالا لشرع الله

IBNKATHIR:87:15/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r2.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r2.claim: A report from Jābir interprets purification as bearing witness that none is god but God, rejecting idols, and affirming Muhammad’s messengership; prayer means the five prayers observed carefully. Al-Bazzār says this is its only route from Jābir.
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r2.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله ، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : { قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكَّى } قال : " من شهد أن لا إله إلا الله

IBNKATHIR:87:15/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse refers to the five daily prayers, a view chosen by Ibn Jarīr.
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r3.anchor: وكذا قال ابن عباس : إن المراد بذلك الصلوات الخمس . واختاره ابن جرير

IBNKATHIR:87:15/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r4.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r4.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya applied the verse to giving zakāt al-fiṭr before Eid prayer; he says Medinans regarded it, along with providing water, as the best charity.
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r4.anchor: حدثنا مروان بن معاوية ، عن أبي خلدة قال : دخلت على أبي العالية فقال لي

IBNKATHIR:87:15/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r5.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r5.claim: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz used to order people to give the charity of breaking the fast and recite this verse.
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r5.anchor: روينا عن أمير المؤمنين عمر بن عبد العزيز أنه كان يأمر الناس بإخراج صدقة الفطر

IBNKATHIR:87:15/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r6.speaker: أبو الأحوص
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r6.claim: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ says a person approached by a supplicant before prayer should give his zakāt before praying, applying this verse.
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r6.anchor: وقال أبو الأحوص : إذا أتى أحدكم سائل وهو يريد الصلاة ، فليقدم بين يدي صلاته زكاته

IBNKATHIR:87:15/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r7.claim: Qatāda glosses the verse as purifying one’s wealth and pleasing one’s Creator.
IBNKATHIR:87:15/r7.anchor: وقال قتادة في هذه الآية { قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكَّى وَذَكَرَ اسْمَ رَبِّهِ فَصَلَّى } زكى ماله وأرضى خالقه

MAWARDI:87:15/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:15/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI:87:15/r1.claim: Remembering the Lord means affirming His oneness.
MAWARDI:87:15/r1.anchor: أحدها : أن يوحد الله ،   قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI:87:15/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:15/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI:87:15/r2.claim: It can mean invoking God and earnestly asking Him.

MAWARDI:87:15/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:15/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI:87:15/r3.claim: It can mean asking God's forgiveness and repenting to Him.

MAWARDI:87:15/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:15/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI:87:15/r4.claim: One remembers God inwardly during prayer, fearing punishment and hoping for reward; the prayer's completeness and humility should match that balance.
MAWARDI:87:15/r4.anchor: الرابع : أن يذكره بقلبه عند صلاته فيخاف عقابه ويرجو ثوابه ،   ليكون استيفاؤه لها وخشوعه فيها بحسب خوفه ورجائه .

MAWARDI:87:15/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:15/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI:87:15/r5.claim: It can mean saying God's name aloud when beginning prayer, since prayer is not valid without invoking Him.
MAWARDI:87:15/r5.anchor: الخامس : أن يذكر اسم ربه بلسانه عند إحرامه بصلاته ،   لأنها لا تنعقد إلا بذكره .

MAWARDI:87:15/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:15/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI:87:15/r6.claim: It can mean beginning each sūra with In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.
MAWARDI:87:15/r6.anchor: أن يفتتح كل سورة ببسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

MAWARDI:87:15/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:15/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI:87:15/r7.claim: Prayer refers to the five prescribed daily prayers.
MAWARDI:87:15/r7.anchor: أحدها : الصلوات الخمس ،   قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI:87:15/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:15/r8.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
MAWARDI:87:15/r8.claim: Prayer refers to the Eid prayer.
MAWARDI:87:15/r8.anchor: الثاني : صلاة العيد{[3249]} ،   قاله أبو سعيد الخدري

MAWARDI:87:15/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:15/r9.speaker: أبو الأحوص
MAWARDI:87:15/r9.claim: Prayer means performing a voluntary prayer after paying alms.
MAWARDI:87:15/r9.anchor: الثالث : هو أن يتطوع بصلاة بعد زكاة ،   قاله أبو الأحوص

MAWARDI:87:15/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:15/r10.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI:87:15/r10.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk reports that the passage was revealed about Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq.
MAWARDI:87:15/r10.anchor: وذكر الضحاك أنها نزلت في أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه

MUQATIL:75:19-21/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:75:19-21/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:75:19-21/r2.claim: Muqatil cites the description of one who purifies himself, remembers God, and prays from al-A'la as a contrast: the Meccan unbelievers do not purify themselves or pray.
MUQATIL:75:19-21/r2.anchor:
قد أفلح من تزكى وذكر اسم ربه فصلى
[الأعلى: 14، 15] يقول الله تعالى في هذه السورة { كلا بل } لا تزكون، ولا تصلون

NASAFI:87:15/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:15/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:87:15/r1.claim: Remembering the Lord’s name means saying the opening takbir, and then praying the five daily prayers.
NASAFI:87:15/r1.anchor: { وَذَكَرَ اسم رَبِّهِ } وكبر للافتتاح { فصلى } الخمس وبه يحتج

NASAFI:87:15/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:15/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:87:15/r2.claim: Nasafi uses the phrase as evidence that the opening takbir is obligatory, is outside the prayer because it is conjoined to it, and may be made with any of God’s names.
NASAFI:87:15/r2.anchor: وبه يحتج على وجوب تكبيرة الافتتاح ، وعلى أنها ليست من الصلاة ، لأن الصلاة عطفت عليها

NASAFI:87:15/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:15/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI:87:15/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the remembrance as recalling one’s return and standing before the Lord, then praying to Him.
NASAFI:87:15/r3.anchor: ذكر معاده وموقفه بين يدي ربه وصلى له

NASAFI:87:15/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:15/r4.speaker: الضحاك
NASAFI:87:15/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says the person mentions God’s name on the way to the prayer ground and performs the Eid prayer.
NASAFI:87:15/r4.anchor: ذكر اسم ربه في طريق المصلى فصلى صلاة العيد

QURTUBI:87:15/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:15/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:15/r1.claim: The phrase means that the person remembered his Lord.

QURTUBI:87:15/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:15/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:87:15/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, in a report through Ata, interprets this as remembering the return and standing before God, then worshipping and praying to Him.
QURTUBI:87:15/r2.anchor: وروى عطاء عن ابن عباس قال : يريد ذكر معاده وموقفه بين يدي اللّه جل ثناؤه ، فعبده وصلى له

QURTUBI:87:15/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:15/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:87:15/r3.claim: One interpretation is that the person says the opening takbir, since prayer is not initiated without invoking God.
QURTUBI:87:15/r3.anchor: وقيل : ذكر اسم ربه بالتكبير في أول الصلاة ، لأنها لا تنعقد إلا بذكره

QURTUBI:87:15/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:15/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:15/r4.claim: This wording is used as evidence that the opening takbir is obligatory and outside the prayer, since prayer is conjoined to it.
QURTUBI:87:15/r4.anchor: وبه يحتج على وجوب تكبيرة الافتتاح ، وعلى أنها ليست من الصلاة ؛ لأن الصلاة معطوفة عليها

QURTUBI:87:15/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:15/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:15/r5.claim: The wording also supports the juristic view that prayer may be opened with any of God's names; jurists disagree on this question.
QURTUBI:87:15/r5.anchor: وفيه حجة لمن قال : إن الافتتاح جائز بكل اسم من أسماء اللّه عز وجل . وهذه مسألة خلافية بين الفقهاء

QURTUBI:87:15/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:15/r6.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI:87:15/r6.claim: Dahhak interprets the remembrance as saying takbir on the way to the prayer ground, followed by the Eid prayer.
QURTUBI:87:15/r6.anchor: قال الضحاك : " وذكر اسم ربه " في طريق المصلى " فصلى " ؛ أي صلاة العيد

QURTUBI:87:15/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:15/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:87:15/r7.claim: Another view is inward remembrance during prayer, fearing punishment and hoping for reward, producing full observance and humility proportionate to hope and fear.
QURTUBI:87:15/r7.anchor: وقيل : " وذكر اسم ربه " وهو أن يذكره بقلبه عند صلاته ، فيخاف عقابه ، ويرجو ثوابه ؛ ليكون استيفاؤه لها ، وخشوعه فيها ، بحسب خوفه ورجائه

QURTUBI:87:15/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:15/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:87:15/r8.claim: Another interpretation is beginning each sura with the formula In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.
QURTUBI:87:15/r8.anchor: وقيل : هو أن يفتتح أول كل سورة ب بسم اللّه الرحمن الرحيم

QURTUBI:87:15/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:15/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:15/r9.claim: The sequence need not be chronological: it can mean that he prayed and remembered, just as Arabic may mention visiting before honoring without fixing order.
QURTUBI:87:15/r9.anchor: " فصلى " أي فصلى وذكر . ولا فرق بين أن تقول : أكرمتني فزرتني ، وبين أن تقول : زرتني فأكرمتني

QURTUBI:87:15/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:15/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:87:15/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says the prayer here is the five obligatory prayers.
QURTUBI:87:15/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس : هذا في الصلاة المفروضة ، وهي الصلوات الخمس

QURTUBI:87:15/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:15/r11.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:87:15/r11.claim: Another view takes the prayer as supplication to God for worldly and afterlife needs.
QURTUBI:87:15/r11.anchor: وقيل : الدعاء ، أي دعاء اللّه بحوائج الدنيا والآخرة

QURTUBI:87:15/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:15/r12.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري وابن عمر
QURTUBI:87:15/r12.claim: Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, Ibn Umar, and others are reported to interpret the prayer as the Eid prayer.
QURTUBI:87:15/r12.anchor: وقيل : صلاة العيد . قاله أبو سعيد الخدري وابن عمر وغيرهما

QURTUBI:87:15/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:15/r13.speaker: أبو الأحوص
QURTUBI:87:15/r13.claim: Abu al-Ahwas interprets it as voluntary prayer after giving zakat; Qurtubi says this fits Ata's view.
QURTUBI:87:15/r13.anchor: وقيل : هو أن يتطوع بصلاة بعد زكاته ، قاله أبو الأحوص ، وهو مقتضى قول عطاء

QURTUBI:87:15/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:15/r14.speaker: عبد الله
QURTUBI:87:15/r14.claim: Abdullah is reported to say that one who establishes prayer but does not give zakat has no prayer.
QURTUBI:87:15/r14.anchor: وروي عن عبد الله قال : من أقام الصلاة ولم يؤت الزكاة فلا صلاة له

RAZI:87:15/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:15/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI:87:15/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets remembering the Lord as remembering one's return and standing before Him, which leads one to pray to Him.
RAZI:87:15/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس : ذكر معاده وموقفه بين يدي ربه فصلى له

RAZI:87:15/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:15/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:87:15/r2.claim: Al-Rāzī prefers Ibn ʿAbbās's reading and organizes religious action into purifying belief, knowing God, and serving Him.
RAZI:87:15/r2.anchor: وأقول : هذا التفسير متعين وذلك لأن مراتب أعمال المكلف ثلاثة

RAZI:87:15/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:15/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:87:15/r4.claim: The second stage is knowing God in His essence, attributes, and names; remembrance in the heart is knowledge.
RAZI:87:15/r4.anchor: وثانيها : هي المراد بقوله : { وذكر اسم ربه } فإن الذكر بالقلب ليس إلا المعرفة

RAZI:87:15/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:15/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:87:15/r5.claim: The third stage is service to God, expressed by prayer as humility and submissiveness.
RAZI:87:15/r5.anchor: وثالثها : الخدمة وهي المراد بقوله : { فصلى } فإن الصلاة عبارة عن التواضع والخشوع

RAZI:87:15/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:15/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:87:15/r6.claim: Knowing God's majesty must show itself in bodily acts of submission and humility.
RAZI:87:15/r6.anchor: فمن استنار قلبه بمعرفة جلال الله تعالى وكبريائه

RAZI:87:15/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:15/r7.speaker: عكرمة وأبو العالية وابن سيرين وابن عمر
RAZI:87:15/r7.claim: These authorities read the passage as giving alms before going to the Eid prayer, then praying Eid with the imam.
RAZI:87:15/r7.anchor: وهذا قول عكرمة وأبي العالية وابن سيرين وابن عمر

RAZI:87:15/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:15/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI:87:15/r8.claim: The Eid-alms and Eid-prayer interpretation is also narrated as a report raised to the Prophet; al-Rāzī states no grading.
RAZI:87:15/r8.anchor: وروي ذلك مرفوعا إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI:87:15/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:15/r9.speaker: author
RAZI:87:15/r9.claim: Al-Rāzī objects that the Eid reading puts alms before prayer, whereas the Qurʾān customarily mentions prayer before zakat.
RAZI:87:15/r9.anchor: أن عادة الله تعالى في القرآن تقديم ذكر الصلاة على ذكر الزكاة لا تقديم الزكاة على الصلاة

RAZI:87:15/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:15/r10.speaker: الثعلبي
RAZI:87:15/r10.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī says the sūra is Meccan by consensus, when neither Eid nor zakat al-fiṭr existed in Mecca; al-Rāzī uses this as an objection.
RAZI:87:15/r10.anchor: قال الثعلبي : هذه السورة مكية بالإجماع ولم يكن بمكة عيد ولا زكاة فطر

RAZI:87:15/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:15/r12.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI:87:15/r12.claim: Muqātil reads purification as giving from one's wealth and remembering God through affirming His oneness in prayer.
RAZI:87:15/r12.anchor: قال مقاتل : { قد أفلح من تزكى } أي تصدق من ماله وذكر ربه بالتوحيد في الصلاة

RAZI:87:15/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:15/r13.speaker: author
RAZI:87:15/r13.claim: Unlike the Eid interpretation, Muqātil's reading concerns the obligatory alms and prayers.
RAZI:87:15/r13.anchor: والفرق بين هذا الوجه وما قبله أن هذا يتناول الزكاة والصلاة المفروضتين

RAZI:87:15/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:15/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI:87:15/r15.claim: A further report from Ibn ʿAbbās takes this as proclaiming God's greatness while setting out for Eid.
RAZI:87:15/r15.anchor: قال ابن عباس : { وذكر اسم ربه } أي كبر في خروجه إلى العيد

RAZI:87:15/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:15/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI:87:15/r16.claim: In that further interpretation, the prayer is the Eid prayer.
RAZI:87:15/r16.anchor: كبر في خروجه إلى العيد وصلى صلاة العيد

RAZI:87:15/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:15/r17.speaker: author
RAZI:87:15/r17.claim: Another interpretation is remembering God during prayer, unlike hypocrites who pray ostentatiously and remember God only rarely.
RAZI:87:15/r17.anchor: المعنى وذكر اسم ربه في صلاته ولا تكون صلاته كصلاة المنافقين

RAZI:87:15/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:15/r18.speaker: الفقهاء
RAZI:87:15/r18.claim: Jurists cite the verse as evidence that the opening takbīr is obligatory.
RAZI:87:15/r18.anchor: الفقهاء احتجوا بهذه الآية على وجوب تكبيرة الافتتاح

RAZI:87:15/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:15/r19.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI:87:15/r19.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa argues that the conjunction separates the opening takbīr from prayer, so it is not part of prayer.
RAZI:87:15/r19.anchor: واحتج أبو حنيفة رحمه الله بها على أن تكبيرة الافتتاح

RAZI:87:15/r20.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:15/r20.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI:87:15/r20.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa also argues that the opening is valid with any of God's names.
RAZI:87:15/r20.anchor: واحتج أيضا بهذه الآية على أن الافتتاح جائز بكل اسم من أسمائه

RAZI:87:15/r21.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:15/r21.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI:87:15/r21.claim: Al-Rāzī's school replies that the wording can be understood as 'he prayed, then remembered God's name'; ordinary speech can reverse the order.

RAZI:87:15/r22.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:15/r22.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI:87:15/r22.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa answers that the sequential force of the fāʾ cannot be set aside without evidence.
RAZI:87:15/r22.anchor: ولأبي حنيفة أن يقول : ترك العمل بفاء التعقيب

RAZI:87:15/r23.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:15/r23.speaker: author
RAZI:87:15/r23.claim: Al-Rāzī's preferred reply is that the verse praises remembering God and then praying, without identifying the remembrance as the opening takbīr.
RAZI:87:15/r23.anchor: الأولى ) في الجواب أن يقال : الآية تدل على مدح كل

RAZI:87:15/r24.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:15/r24.speaker: author
RAZI:87:15/r24.claim: The remembrance may instead be inward recollection of God's reward and punishment, which prompts prayer; takbīr is then one component of the prayer.
RAZI:87:15/r24.anchor: فلعل المراد به أن من ذكر الله بقلبه وذكر ثوابه وعقابه دعاه ذلك إلى فعل الصلاة

QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r22.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r22.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r22.claim: The verse can mean remembering God's name in prayer, or affirming His oneness and praying to Him.
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r22.anchor: ذكر اسم ربه في صلاته . ويقال : ذكره بالوحدانية

FARRA:v3p256/r13.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p256/r13.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p256/r13.claim: Remembering God's name and praying can mean attending prayer with the imam.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r2.claim: The fortunate attain success by purification, remembering their Lord, and prayer.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r2.anchor: Glad tidings of success are given to the fortunate who

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p279/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p279/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p279/r4.claim: Those who benefited from the Prophet's reminders purify themselves from polytheism and disbelief and receive success and God's pleasure in both lives.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p280/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p280/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p280/r1.claim: Remembering God's name and praying are purification's foremost expression and method; prayer manifests belief, which grounds and guards the Sharīʿah's directives.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p280/r1.anchor: manifestation of belief in the Almighty

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r9.claim: Remembering the Lord's name means affirming His oneness; prayer includes obligatory worship and whatever supererogatory worship one can manage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r9.anchor: وذكر اسم ربه: أي وحده، لم يقرنه بشيء من الأنداد، فصلى: أي أتى الصلاة المفروضة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r11.claim: He calls weak the argument that the verse proves the opening takbīr is obligatory, may use any divine name, and lies outside prayer because prayer is conjoined to it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r11.anchor: واحتج بقوله: وذكر اسم ربه على وجوب تكبيرة الافتتاح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says remembering the Lord's name means remembering the return and standing before Him, then praying to Him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r12.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: وذكر اسم ربه: أي معاده وموقفه بين يدي ربه

DURR-FULL:v8p483/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p483/r8.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
DURR-FULL:v8p483/r8.claim: The Prophet glosses purification as affirming God's oneness, rejecting idols, and testifying that he is God's Messenger; prayer is the five prayers observed at their times.
DURR-FULL:v8p483/r8.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: في قوله: {قد أفلح من تزكى}

DURR-FULL:v8p483/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p483/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p483/r9.claim: Purification means freedom from associating partners; remembrance means affirming God's oneness; prayer means the five daily prayers.
DURR-FULL:v8p483/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {قد أفلح من تزكى} قال: من الشرك

STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r2.speaker: family of the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r2.claim: One view dates the opening Makkan and the ending Madinan because these verses refer to Eid al-Fiṭr prayer and alms, institutionalized in Medina.
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r2.anchor: from the family of the Prophet, refer to “the prayer and zakāh
